Ltd. — Referred to as supporting the same approach adopted in SSP Aviation and RRJ Securities. 6. RKM Powergen (P.) Ltd. — Its contrary reasoning restricting the Section 153C(1) proviso to abatement was not sustained in Ojjus Medicare in view of Jasjit Singh. 7. A.R. Safiullah — Cited with approval in Ojjus Medicare on computation of the statutory ten-assessment-year outer limit. FULL TEXT OF THE ORDER OF ITAT DELHI 1. Advertisement (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({}); Jaswant Singh @ Rolly Babu Vs Union of India (Patna High Court) Summary: The Patna High Court considered the regular bail application of Shri Jaswant Singh @ Rolly Babu in connection with Complaint Case No. 49 of 2026, arising from allegations under Section 132(1)(a), (b), (c) and (d) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017. The petitioner was arrested following summons/interrogation in a CGST complaint concerning alleged tax evasion and fraudulent transactions. The prosecution alleged that the petitioner issued tax invoices to multiple beneficiary firms without actual physical movement or supply of goods, fraudulently availed input tax credit without actual receipt of goods or services and without corresponding e-way bills, falsified accounts and financial records, and abetted and operated shell entities by controlling GST credentials, banking operations, passwords and compliance activities. The alleged revenue implication was approximately Rs. 73.75 crores. The petitioner denied the allegations and contended that his arrest was based merely on suspicion and without the requisite “reason to believe”. He argued that the allegations principally rested upon statements of proprietors of other firms and co-accused persons, without giving him an opportunity for cross-examination. He also submitted that the allegation concerning control of GST credentials was incorrect, that no incriminating material, notebook or diary was found during the search of his residence, and that the filing of returns and other forms had been handled by his accountant. According to the petitioner, investigation of the relevant IP address would be necessary before attributing responsibility for electronic filings. Reliance was placed on Section 69 of the CGST Act, 2017, under which the Commissioner must have reasons to believe that the person has committed specified offences under Section 132 before authorising arrest. The petitioner argued that the arrest authorisation and arrest memo did not disclose the requisite reason to believe or the monetary threshold relevant to the alleged offence. He also relied upon Section 132 of the CGST Act, 2017 concerning offences and punishment. The petitioner relied upon Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar and Anr. and reproduced the Supreme Court’s directions requiring arrest to be preceded by consideration of necessity and appropriate reasons and requiring Magistrates to scrutinise the basis for detention. Reliance was also placed on Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation and Anr., including the principles concerning arrest under Section 35 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. The petitioner further relied upon State of Punjab v. Davinder Pal Singh Bhullar, Radhika Agarwal v. Union of India, Andaman Timber Industries v. CCE, Shri Mukesh Agarwal v. UOI and Sanket Mittal v. Central GST Department. He emphasised that the investigation had been completed and the charge sheet filed, that there was no possibility of tampering with evidence, and that he had remained in judicial custody since 26.05.2026. The Union of India opposed bail, submitting that the matter involved an economic offence which should be dealt with sternly. It referred to the punishment prescribed under Section 132 for wrongly availed or utilised input tax credit or refund exceeding the statutory thresholds, submitting that where the amount exceeded Rs. 5 crores, the punishment could extend to five years. Having heard the parties and considered the facts and circumstances, the Patna High Court was inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail. The Court directed his release in Complaint Case No. 49 of 2026 upon furnishing a bail bond of Rs.10,000/- with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Special Judge, Economic Offence, Patna/Concerned Court, Patna. The order therefore resulted in grant of regular bail to the petitioner; it did not finally adjudicate the allegations concerning fake invoices, fraudulent input tax credit, falsification of records or operation of shell entities. Davinder Pal Singh Bhullar & Others, (2011) 14 SCC 770. Radhika Agarwal v. Union of India & Others, 2025 INSC 247; W.P. (Crl.) No. 336 of 2018. Andaman Timber Industries v. rows.title: Goods and Services Tax | GST Notice Only Under Additional Notices Tab Violates Natural Justice: Calcutta HC
rows.desc: Case Law Details TaxGuru Citation 2026 taxguru.in 12582 Case Name Subhra Baral Vs Deputy Commissioner of Revenue (Calcutta High Court) Appeal Number Only available for paid members Date of Judgement/Order Only available for paid members Courts All High Courts, Calcutta High Court Upgrade to Basic or Premium to download. Already Upgraded? Log in. Advertisement (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({}); Subhra Baral Vs Deputy Commissioner of Revenue (Calcutta High Court) Summary: The Calcutta High Court allowed the writ petition filed by Subhra Baral challenging the adjudication order dated 28.07.2024 and the appellate order dated 29.05.2025 passed under Section 107 of the West Bengal Goods and Services Tax Act and Section 107 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, whereby the petitioner’s appeal had been dismissed solely on limitation. The petitioner submitted that Show Cause Notice in Form GST DRC-01 No. ZD190524017416E dated 12.05.2024, demanding tax, interest and penalty, had been uploaded on the GST portal only under the “Additional Notice and Orders” tab. According to the petitioner, no separate intimation was received, due to which the notice remained unnoticed and no reply could be filed. The petitioner stated that the adjudication order dated 28.07.2024 came to his knowledge only when his accountant checked the common portal in March 2025. The appeal filed thereafter under Section 107 was dismissed on limitation without examination on merits. The State contended that ample opportunities had been granted and the appeal was correctly rejected as time-barred. The High Court, however, found that the petitioner had made out a prima facie case. It specifically observed that uploading the show cause notice only under the “Additional Notice and Orders” tab without separate intimation had prevented the petitioner from replying and constituted a violation of natural justice. Since the appellate authority had dismissed the appeal only on limitation and had not considered the merits, the Court held that interference was warranted in the peculiar facts of the case. The High Court consequently quashed and set aside both the appellate order dated 29.05.2025 and the adjudication order dated 28.07.2024, and also quashed the consequential bank attachment. Respondent No.1 was directed to revisit the issue by considering on merits the grounds taken in the petitioner’s appeal, grant an opportunity of hearing and pass a fresh reasoned adjudication order in accordance with law within 12 weeks. The decision was directed to be communicated to the petitioner within one week thereafter. The writ petition was accordingly disposed of. FULL TEXT OF THE CALCUTTA HIGH COURT ORDER 1. Affidavit of service filed in Court today be kept with the record. 2. The present petition has been filed challenging inter alia, the legality and validity of the adjudication order dated 28.07.2024 passed by the respondent No.1 and the appellate order dated 29th May, 2025 passed by the respondent no.2 under Section 107 of the West Bengal Goods and Services Tax Act(hereinafter referred to as the said ‘WBGST Act’) and the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (hereinafter referred to as the said ‘CGST Act’), whereby the appeal of the petitioner has been dismissed on ground of limitation. 3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits as follows; i. That a show cause notice in Form DRC 01 No. ZD190524017416E dated 12.05.2024 has been issued to the petitioner demanding tax, interest and penalty. ii. That said notice has been uploaded on the GST portal under the tab ‘Additional Notice and Orders’. Due to this, the petitioner did not get any actual intimation and hence could not respond to the show cause notice. iii. That the petitioner came to know above the adjudication order dated 28.07.2024 only after the accountant checked the common portal in the month of March, 2025. iv. That the petitioner preferred an appeal before the appellate authority under Section 107 of the said Act but the same has been dismissed solely on the ground of limitation, without considering the merits. v. That the entire proceedings and the impugned order are contrary to law and have been passed in violation of principles of natural justice and without due compliance with the procedure prescribed under the said Act. 4. Learned counsel appearing for the State respondents opposed the writ petition and submitted since the petitioner has been granted ample opportunities to defend his case, the appeal has been rightly dismissed on limitation. 5. Having heard the parties and upon perusing the records made available this Court observes as follows; i. The petitioner has been able to make a prima facie case. ii. The fact that show cause notice has been only uploaded under the ‘tab Additional Notice and Orders’ and no separate intimation has been given therefore the petitioner has been unable to reply to the same. This constitutes a violation of natural justice. 6. Since

rows.title: Corporate Law | Sports Centre Building Tax Exemption Claim Requires Reconsideration: Kerala HC
rows.desc: Case Law Details TaxGuru Citation 2026 taxguru.in 12581 Case Name Regional Sports Centre Vs State of Kerala (Kerala High Court) Appeal Number Only available for paid members Date of Judgement/Order Only available for paid members Courts All High Courts, Kerala High Court Upgrade to Basic or Premium to download. Already Upgraded? Log in. Advertisement (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({}); Regional Sports Centre Vs State of Kerala (Kerala High Court) Summary: The Kerala High Court set aside the Kerala Government’s order dated 25.04.2023 rejecting Regional Sports Centre, Cochin’s claim for exemption from building tax and directed fresh consideration of whether its buildings were principally used for charitable purposes under Section 3(1)(b) of the Kerala Building Tax Act, 1975. The petitioner, a society registered under the Travancore Cochin Literary, Scientific and Charitable Societies Registration Act, 1955, operated a sports complex in Cochin and claimed to provide training facilities in 33 sports. It sought exemption on the ground that its buildings were principally used for charitable and educational purposes. The petitioner also relied upon exemptions/registrations granted under Section 12A and Section 80G of the Income Tax Act, 1961 and contended that promotion of sports constituted an object of general public utility without profit motive. The Government opposed the claim, pointing to membership, user and coaching fees and contending that free training was extended only to four persons. On the claim of “educational purposes”, the High Court referred to Sole Trustee, Loka Shikshana Trust v. Commissioner of Income Tax, Mysore and Assistant Commissioner of Income-Tax (Exemptions) v. Ahmedabad Urban Development Authority and held that sports promotion could not be brought within “education” in the relevant sense. The Court, however, found that the claim under “charitable purposes” required reconsideration. The Government’s conclusion that free training was given only to four persons did not adequately account for Ext.P7, which showed free coaching being provided to various persons in different sports, including on recommendations of MPs, MLAs and Councillors. Referring to Government of Kerala v. Mother Superior, the Court emphasized that exemption under Section 3(1)(b) depends upon the principal use of the building and does not require exclusive use for the exempt purpose. It also referred to Lissy Medical Institutions v. State of Kerala, which held that Explanation I to Section 3(1) was not confined to relief of the poor and free medical relief because the provision used the expression “includes”. The High Court therefore set aside Ext.P11 and directed the Government to reconsider the exemption claim, grant the petitioner an opportunity of hearing and pass fresh orders within six months. All coercive proceedings were directed to remain in abeyance until fresh orders were issued. Cases Discussed / Relied Upon Sole Trustee, Loka Shikshana Trust v. Commissioner of Income Tax, Mysore [(1976) 1 SCC 254] (Supreme Court) — referred to while considering whether sports promotion could qualify as “education”. The Supreme Court’s restricted meaning of education as systematic instruction, schooling or training was applied while rejecting the petitioner’s claim under the “educational purposes” limb. Assistant Commissioner of Income-Tax (Exemptions) v. Ahmedabad Urban Development Authority [2022 449 ITR 1 (SC)] — referred to for the position that a sports association’s activity does not fall within “education” under Section 2(15) of the Income Tax Act. The High Court relied on this along with Sole Trustee, Loka Shikshana Trust while holding that the petitioner may not claim the building-tax exemption under the heading “educational purposes”. Government of Kerala v. Mother Superior [2021 (2) KLT 270 (SC)] — relied upon for the principle that exemption based on buildings used “principally for” specified purposes turns on their principal use rather than ownership and does not require exclusive use for the exempt purpose. Lissy Medical Institutions v. State of Kerala and Others [(2024) 1 SCC 200] (Supreme Court) — referred to for the proposition that Explanation I to Section 3(1) of the Kerala Building Tax Act is not confined to relief of the poor and free medical relief, having regard to the use of the expression “includes”. rows.desc: Case Law Details TaxGuru Citation 2026 taxguru.in 12580 Case Name Mayur Timber Vs State of Rajasthan & Ors. (Rajasthan High Court) Appeal Number Only available for paid members Date of Judgement/Order Only available for paid members Courts All High Courts, Rajasthan High Court Upgrade to Basic or Premium to download. Already Upgraded? Log in. Advertisement (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({}); Mayur Timber Vs State of Rajasthan & Ors. (Rajasthan High Court) Summary: The Rajasthan High Court allowed the writ petition filed by M/s Mayur Timber challenging the show-cause notice dated 13.06.2024 and consequential order dated 15.10.2024 passed under Section 74 of the CGST Act, 2017, whereby GST demand of Rs.3,13,894, interest of Rs.4,26,002 and penalty of Rs.3,13,894 had been confirmed on the allegation of ITC availment without actual receipt of goods. The Court found that the show-cause notice, reminder and adjudication order bore neither digital nor physical signatures. Examining Rule 26(3) of the CGST Rules, 2017, the Court held that electronic issuance and authentication are distinct and cumulative requirements and that mere generation of a document on the GST portal or allotment of a reference number cannot substitute authentication by signature. A signature authenticates the document, fixes accountability on the issuing officer and safeguards against arbitrariness by evidencing application of mind. Consequently, an unsigned show-cause notice or order is no notice or order in the eyes of law, and the defect is not a curable irregularity but goes to the root of the authority to proceed. The Court further noted that the documents had been uploaded only under “Additional Notices and Orders”, the petitioner learnt about the demand only upon bank recovery proceedings, and no effective personal hearing had been afforded contrary to Section 75(4). The plea of alternative remedy was therefore rejected. The show-cause notice, consequential order dated 15.10.2024 and recovery notice in FORM GST DRC-13 dated 20.08.2025 were set aside, while liberty was granted to the respondents to proceed afresh through a duly authenticated show-cause notice and after providing an effective opportunity of hearing. The Court expressly left all issues on the merits of the tax demand open. FULL TEXT OF THE JUDGMENT/ORDER OF RAJASTHAN HIGH COURT 1. The petitioner herein seeks quashing of the impugned show-cause notice dated 13.06.2024 and the consequent order dated 15.10.2024 passed under Section 74 of the CGST Act, 2017, whereby a demand of Rs.3,13,894/- along with interest and penalty has been raised against the petitioner. 2. Brief facts of the case are as follows. The petitioner has filed the present writ petition challenging the order dated 15.10.2024 passed by respondent No.3 under Section 74 of the CGST Act, 2017 read with FORM GST DRC-07. By the said order, a demand of Rs.3,13,894 towards GST was confirmed against the petitioner. Interest of Rs.4,26,002 and penalty of Rs.3,13,894 were also confirmed. Prior thereto, an unsigned (as alleged) FORM GST DRC-01 (Summary of Show Cause Notice) along with the Show Cause Notice dated 13.06.2024 was issued on the GST portal. The allegation was that the petitioner had availed ITC of Rs.3,13,894 without actual receipt of goods. 2.1 The impugned order was uploaded on the GST portal on 15.10.2024. It was uploaded under the head “Additional Notices and Orders” and not under “Notices and Orders”. It is stated that the order was never served upon the petitioner manually or in hard copy. It is further stated that no opportunity of personal hearing was afforded to the petitioner before the impugned order was passed. 2.2 Subsequently, on 20.08.2025, respondent No.3 issued FORM GST DRC-13 under Section 79(1)(c) of the CGST Act to the Manager, Kotak Mahindra Bank. rows.desc: CompaniesLIC Gets RBI Approval To Raise ICICI Bank Stake To 9.99%; Key DetailsEdited by: Priya RaghuvanshiUpdated Sep 5, 2026, 17:52 ISTLIC has received Reserve Bank of India approval to acquire up to 9.99 per cent in ICICI Bank, with the permission valid for one year from September 4.According to the exchange filing, ICICI Bank received the RBI’s approval letter dated September 4, 2026. (File Photo)follow usfollow us.Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) has secured approval from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to acquire up to 9.99 per cent of the paid-up share capital or voting rights in ICICI Bank, according to a regulatory filing by the private sector lender. The approval gives the state-owned insurer one year from the date of the RBI’s letter to complete the proposed acquisition. The permission will cease to remain valid if LIC does not acquire the stake within the prescribed period.ICICI Bank said it received the RBI communication on September 4, 2026, at 9:09 pm. The proposed stake purchase will also have to comply with all applicable statutory and regulatory requirements.According to ICICI Bank’s exchange filing, the RBI has permitted LIC to build an “aggregate holding” of as much as 9.99 per cent in the bank.“On September 4, 2026 at 9:09 pm, ICICI Bank Limited (the Bank) has received a copy of Reserve Bank of India (RBI ) letter dated the same day addressed to Life Insurance Corporation of India (the applicant) that it has accorded its approval to the applicant to acquire ‘aggregate holding’ of up to 9.9 9 per cent of the paid -up share capital or voting rights in the Bank within one year from the date of RBI approval letter, failing which RBI approval shall stand cancelled.”The filing further clarified that the regulatory permission comes with conditions governing the transaction.“The approval is subject to certain conditions including compliance with the relevant statutory and regulatory provisions,” the filing read.This means any increase in LIC’s holding will remain subject to the broader rules applicable to shareholding in regulated banking entities.LIC Expands Presence Across Major BanksThe RBI approval for ICICI Bank comes shortly after LIC received clearance to increase its holding in another major private lender, HDFC Bank.In an August 19 regulatory filing, HDFC Bank disclosed that the RBI had approved LIC’s application to acquire up to 9.99 per cent of its paid-up share capital or voting rights.The filing stated that the regulator had “accorded its approval to Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC)” to acquire the additional stake in the bank.HDFC Bank also disclosed LIC’s existing ownership position, stating that LIC "holds 4.11% of the total share capital of the Bank."The latest approvals underline LIC’s growing presence as a significant institutional investor in India’s banking sector, particularly among the country’s largest private lenders.What The ICICI Bank Approval MeansThe RBI clearance does not by itself indicate that LIC will immediately purchase the entire 9.99 per cent permitted stake. Instead, it provides the insurer with regulatory authorisation to build its holding up to that level during the one-year approval period.The final extent and timing of any acquisition will therefore depend on LIC’s investment decisions and compliance with applicable regulations.For ICICI Bank, the approval provides clarity on LIC’s ability to increase its ownership in the lender while placing the transaction within the regulatory framework governing significant shareholdings in banks.The development also comes as institutional investors continue to play a prominent role in India’s financial sector, with large insurers and other long-term investors holding stakes in leading banking companies.(With Agency Inputs)Latest News sportsPickleball World Cup: Purvansh Patel Clinches U-18 Boys Singles GoldcityGerman Shepherd Bites Ahmedabad Woman For 2nd Time In 4 Months, FIR Filed Against Dog OwnersportsSuresh Raina Reveals How One Week With Sachin Tendulkar At BKC Transformed Him, Led To Iconic 'Believe Tattoo'educationShobhit Nirwan On Why Talent Alone Doesn’t Pay: 3 Skills You Need To Actually Make Moneyentertainment newsThe Last Of Us Co-Creator, Naughty Dog No Longer 'Involved' In Making Of Season 3 Of HBO SerieseducationTeachers in Karnataka Can Now Use ‘Tr’ Before Their Names, Says CM ShivakumareducationTeachers’ Day 2026: President Murmu Writes on Teachers, Recalls Her Own Journey as Student and EducatorworldPutin Orders Three-Day Pause on Kyiv Strikes As Witkoff, Kushner Arrive In MoscowPriya Raghuvanshi authorShe is working as a Chief Copy Editor at Times Now’s Business Desk, where she covers key developments in the stock market, Indian corporates across se... rows.title: CBI Files Case Against Subhash Chandra, Others Over Alleged Rs 1,322 Cr LIC Housing Finance FraudSep 5, 2026, 14:06 IST
rows.desc: CompaniesCBI Files Case Against Subhash Chandra, Others Over Alleged Rs 1,322 Cr LIC Housing Finance FraudReported by: Bhavatosh SinghUpdated Sep 5, 2026, 14:06 ISTCBI books Subhash Chandra and three others over alleged cheating involving more than Rs 1,322 crore in LIC Housing Finance loans.Subhash Chandra (File Photo) follow usfollow usThe Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has registered a criminal case against Essel Group Chairman Subhash Chandra and three others over alleged financial fraud involving more than Rs 1,322 crore owed to LIC Housing Finance Ltd (LICHFL). The case follows a complaint filed by LICHFL, which has accused Chandra, Pankaj Suroliya, Amish Pandya and Rajeev Dholakia of allegedly cheating the housing finance company and conspiring to secure credit facilities on the basis of disputed financial disclosures.According to the complaint, Chandra submitted a net worth certificate in 2018 declaring his net worth at Rs 59,113 crore. LICHFL has alleged that the certificate was used to obtain loan facilities for M/s Vasant Sagar Properties Pvt Ltd and other companies linked to him.Relying on the financial certificate, LICHFL subsequently extended credit facilities to three companies associated with Chandra, the complaint stated.The housing finance company has now raised objections over Chandra's statements made during subsequent insolvency proceedings, particularly his denial that he had ever possessed a net worth of Rs 50,000 crore, as reflected in the certificates submitted to LICHFL.LICHFL has alleged cheating, criminal breach of trust and conspiracy in its complaint to the investigating agency.The complaint given to the CBI Head Office reads, "A loan facility of Rs. 500 Crores to Vasant Sagar Properties Pvt. Ltd. and Pan India Infra projects Pvt. Ltd. (Co-borrower) as a Home Entity Loan (Takeover & Top-up for Business Expansion) under Loan Account No. 610700003341 secured by a Letter of Continuing Guarantee dated 28th March 18 executed by Subhash Chandra (Vasant Sagar Loan Facility) and a loan facility of Rs. 480 Crores to Digital Subscriber Management and Consultancy Services Pvt. Ltd. and Spirit Infra power and Multi Ventures Pvt. Ltd. (Co-borrower) as a Rental Discounting facility under the Scheme of Rental Securitization under Loan Account No. 610700003500 secured by a Letter of Continuing Guarantee dated 10th August 18 executed by Subhash Chandra (Digital Loan Facility).""The Vasant Sagar Loan Facility was granted inter alia on the basis of the Net Worth Certificate submitted by Subhash Chandra, issued by 28th March 2018 issued by DIM & Co, certifying that his networth was US$ 6,197.62 Million (approximately Rs. 59,113.21 Crores), as on 31st March 2017 Similarly. the Digital Loan Facility was granted inter alia on the basis of the Net Worth Certificate submitted by Subhash Chandra, issued by MPJ & Co.. Chartered Accountants on 06.07.2018, certifying that his networth was Rs. 40,562 Crores," it added."Thereafter, defaults have occurred in the Vasant Sagar Loan Facility and Digital Loan Facility. In the course of the subsequent proceedings under the Insolvency & Bankruptcy Code, 2016 for the personal insolvency resolution of Subhash Chandra, he categorically denied having the Net Worth as stated in the Net Worth Certificates, which he had submitted to LICHFL to cause approval and disbursal of the loan detailed above," the complaint states."In the course of the proceedings. he has stated that his net worth in 2024 is Rs. 31.79 crore and stated that, even in 2017-18. he did not have the net worth of more than Rs. 40.000 Crores," it noted.Subhash Chandra’s Statement In Insolvency ProceedingsMeanwhile, on 27th August, Zee Group founder Subhash Chandra, in a statement, claimed he has not borrowed any money from any lender and is only a personal guarantor. Total claim against him as a Personal Guarantor, in the personal insolvency proceedings, is only Rs 3,992 crore by the objectors (creditors who had rejected the plan) of the plan and not Rs 22,000 crore (which is the total claim), out of which Rs 21,696 crore was admitted by the Resolution Professional. “Out of which (Rs 3,992 crore), also a claim of Rs 620 crore has been settled and further Rs 1,063 crore offered to be paid by the borrower entities,” Chandra said. rows.title: RBI May Resume Rate Hikes In H2 FY27; Union Bank Sees Repo Rate Rising To 6%Sep 4, 2026, 14:10 IST
rows.desc: EconomyRBI May Resume Rate Hikes In H2 FY27; Union Bank Sees Repo Rate Rising To 6%Edited by: Priya RaghuvanshiUpdated Sep 4, 2026, 14:10 ISTUnion Bank expects RBI to raise the repo rate to 5.75-6 per cent in FY27 as liquidity surges and inflation risks rise, with hikes possible from December.Reserve Bank of India (File Photo)Photo : iStockfollow usfollow usThe Reserve Bank of India (RBI) may have to return to monetary tightening in the second half of FY27 as strong economic activity, elevated inflation risks and a surge in banking-system liquidity create fresh policy challenges, according to an assessment by Union Bank of India (UBI). UBI expects the central bank to potentially lift the repo rate by 50-75 basis points from its current 5.25 per cent level. The anticipated increase could come through two or three hikes of 25 basis points each, taking the benchmark rate to a range of 5.75-6 per cent.The bank's base-case view places the beginning of the potential tightening cycle in December, although it has not completely ruled out an earlier move depending on global developments and domestic liquidity conditions.The outlook reflects a combination of factors that could put pressure on the RBI to recalibrate its monetary policy stance. Strong economic growth, a possible pickup in inflation and tighter financial conditions globally are among the key considerations highlighted by UBI.“Rate hikes are back on the table for H2 FY27,” the report said, adding that December appears to be the more likely starting point in its base-case scenario.The assessment marks a shift in the interest-rate outlook, particularly as the RBI has been dealing with a substantial increase in system liquidity. If excess funds remain within the banking system for an extended period, managing liquidity could become increasingly important for the central bank.Forex Inflows Fuel Surge In Banking LiquidityA major factor behind the liquidity build-up has been the significant foreign exchange inflows associated with the RBI's special swap facility.As of August 31, these inflows had reached around USD 136 billion. FCNR(B) deposits accounted for approximately USD 127.23 billion, while overseas foreign currency borrowings and external commercial borrowings made up the balance.The resulting increase in liquidity has been visible in core liquidity levels. According to UBI, core liquidity climbed from Rs 4.82 lakh crore in mid-June to Rs 8.05 lakh crore by mid-August, with the foreign exchange impact accounting for almost all of the increase.The bank's illustrative scenario points to an even sharper rise, with core liquidity potentially reaching around Rs 14.17 lakh crore by September 11.“After getting dollar flows, now Rupee liquidity management is key policy challenge for RBI,” the report said.RBI May Use Liquidity Tools Before Raising RatesUBI expects the RBI to first focus on absorbing surplus liquidity rather than immediately relying on the repo rate as its primary tool.The central bank could announce liquidity-absorption measures ahead of its October monetary policy review. Among the options identified by UBI are short-duration and longer-duration variable rate reverse repo operations (VRRR), along with an incremental cash reserve ratio (I-CRR).The RBI could also consider bond sales and foreign exchange swaps as additional ways of managing the surplus.UBI believes temporary measures may initially be preferable because they can be rolled back as credit demand improves during the second half of FY27. The bank estimates that the RBI could use a roughly 50:50 combination of short-term VRRR operations and longer-duration measures to tackle the projected liquidity surplus.October Rate Increase Still PossibleAlthough December is UBI's preferred starting point for a rate-hike cycle, an October increase remains possible under certain circumstances.The bank said an earlier hike could come into consideration if the US Federal Reserve increases interest rates in September and the RBI has already addressed excess domestic liquidity through more durable measures.Oil prices are another factor that could influence the central bank's decision. UBI noted that crude prices above USD 90 per barrel could intensify inflationary pressures and put additional strain on the rupee.At the same time, a reduction in geopolitical tensions could provide the RBI with greater room to manoeuvre on monetary policy.Get Latest News Live on Times Now along with Breaking News and Top Headlines from Business, Economy and around the World.Latest News indiaPIL Filed In Uttarakhand HC in Mallikarjun Kharge Venue 'Purification Ritual' Row, Seeks Preservation of Documentary EvidenceworldUS, UK, France & Germany Draft UN Resolution To Refer Iran Over Nuclear BreachesworldJudge Indira Talwani Extends Block on Trump's Mail-In Voting Restrictions Through Election DayworldChina Tightens Information Grip After Deadly Floods Along Nepal Border, Victims Remain UnknownworldDrone Over San Diego Airpo

Read Today's Paper var _BL_pg = 0;var competitionClients = ''; var showFullWidthArticle = '1'; var crrArtId = '133755358'; India's balance of payments likely to post $60-65 bn surplus in FY27 despite wider CAD: HDFC BankSECTIONSIndia's balance of payments likely to post $60-65 bn surplus in FY27 despite wider CAD: HDFC BankANILast Updated: Sep 04, 2026, 12:47:00 PM ISTRate StoryFollow usShareFont SizeAbcSmallAbcMediumAbcLargeSavePrintSynopsisIndia’s balance of payments (BoP) is likely to post a $60-65 billion surplus in FY27, despite a widening current account deficit, HDFC Bank said.ANIIndia’s BoP likely to post USD 60-65 bn surplus in FY27 despite wider CAD: HDFC BankNew Delhi [India], September 4 (ANI): India's balance of payments (BoP) is expected to post a surplus of USD 60-65 billion in FY27 despite a widening current account deficit, as strong inflows through special RBI schemes are likely to offset weak capital flows, HDFC Bank said in a report. #sr_widget.onDemand p, #stock_pro.onDemand p{font-size: 14px;line-height: 1.28;} .onDemand .live_stock{left:17px;padding:1px 3px 1px 5px;font-size:12px;font-weight:600;line-height:18px;top:9px} #sr_widget.onDemand .sr_desc{margin:0 auto 0;} #sr_widget.onDemand .live_stock p a{color: #fff;;} #sr_widget.onDemand .sr_desc{color: #024d99;margin-top:10px;} #sr_widget.onDemand .crypto .live_stock .lb-icon{8px 6px 5px 3px !important} #sr_widget.crypto.onDemand a.text{border-bottom:1px solid #ccc;padding-bottom:5px;display:block;width:100%} #sr_widget.onDemand .sr_desc .text p, #stock_pro.onDemand .sr_desc .text p{font-size:12px;font-weight:400;} The bank expects the current account deficit (CAD) to widen to around 1.1-1.3 per cent of GDP in FY27, with the deficit in the second quarter projected at 1.5-1.7 per cent of GDP. However, it has maintained an upside bias to its BoP surplus forecast. .bgBig{border-bottom:0;padding:20px 0 0 0;} .bgBig a.bglink{font-family:Faustina;font-size:20px;font-style:normal;font-weight:600;line-height:normal;border-bottom:0;} "The large inflows mobilised under the RBI's FCNR(B) deposit and overseas borrowing measures are likely to more than compensate for the weak capital flows recorded in Q1 and support an overall BoP surplus in FY27," HDFC Bank said in its report.According to recent data released by RBI, as of August 31, total foreign exchange inflows under the RBI's special USD-INR swap facility stood at USD 136.38 billion, including USD 127.23 billion through FCNR(B) deposits, USD 5.26 billion under overseas foreign currency borrowings (OFCBs) and USD 3.89 billion through external commercial borrowings (ECBs).India's BoP recorded a deficit of USD 8.1 billion in the first quarter, compared with a surplus of USD 4.5 billion a year earlier. } } Home / Markets / Mutual Fund / MFs pour ₹12,944 cr into 2026 IPOs as institutional concentration deepensMFs pour ₹12,944 cr into 2026 IPOs as institutional concentration deepensICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, SBI Mutual Fund and Nippon India Mutual Fund accounted for over 52 per cent of total institutional allocationsThree fund houses — ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, SBI Mutual Fund and Nippon India Mutual Fund — captured over 52 per cent of total institutional allocations.Shilpa Rangarajan Mumbai 2 min read Last Updated : Sep 06 2026 | 1:58 PM IST @media (min-width:1100px) and (max-width:1280px) { .storymeta .meta-info { flex: 0 0 45%; } } Listen to This ArticleIndia’s mutual fund industry deployed ₹12,944 crore across 2026 mainboard initial public offerings (IPOs), marked by sharp institutional concentration among a few dominant asset managers. Three fund houses — ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, SBI Mutual Fund and Nippon India Mutual Fund — captured over 52 per cent of total institutional allocations, committing ₹6,770 crore to public issues. ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund emerged as the largest overall institutional buyer by absolute value, deploying capital across 13 distinct mainboard listings. However, SBI Mutual Fund established the highest market-cap-weighted ownership position at 3.8 per cent despite participating in only six companies. By consolidating significant capital into a select group of offerings, SBI Mutual Fund demonstrated a targeted strategy that maximised portfolio exposure relative to issuer size. The concentrated backing of major fund houses closely aligned with the market's strongest primary performances. Top-performing listings of the year, including Shadowfax, Amagi, Omnitech and Sedemac Mechatronics, were heavily anchored by these leading institutional buyers. Large fund houses effectively acted as key valuation anchors, providing crucial liquidity and institutional validation during market price discovery. The broader institutional landscape revealed an asymmetric appetite for new paper. While smaller asset managers scattered capital across smaller tickets, dominant fund managers leveraged robust liquidity to secure substantial anchor portions. As primary issuance momentum continues through 2026, asset size and concentrated stock selection remain the primary drivers shaping institutional ownership across India's equity capital markets. (Photo:PTI)Press Trust of India New Delhi 3 min read Last Updated : Sep 06 2026 | 1:45 PM IST @media (min-width:1100px) and (max-width:1280px) { .storymeta .meta-info { flex: 0 0 45%; } } Listen to This ArticleThe government has sold about 4,000 tonnes of buffer onions across 17 cities in the first ten days of a subsidised sale aimed at curbing skyrocketing prices, Consumer Affairs Secretary Nidhi Khare said on Sunday.The Centre, through its agencies NCCF and Nafed, is sitting on a buffer stock of 1.21 lakh tonnes of onion for 2026.These agencies are transporting the stored onions in bulk from producing states to consuming centres, either by a dedicated rail rake christened "Kanda Express" or by trucks, as part of a retail intervention aimed at cooling prices. Credit cards set for wider UPI-led adoption, says report
rows.desc: Articles 2 min read Credit cards set for wider UPI-led adoption, says report The integration of credit cards with UPI is expected to increase utilisation, particularly in ecommerce and higher-value spending, while UPI-powered digital wallets continue to be widely used for day-to-day transactions. ETBFSI Research ETBFSI Published On Sep 5, 2026 at 08:41 AM IST Read by 100 Professionals var news_msid = 133785799; console.log(news_msid); Select ETBFSI as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook India’s credit card usage is expected to grow as integration with the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) expands the use of cards, allowing consumers to make payments through widely accepted UPI QR codes and at merchants without traditional point-of-sale infrastructure, according to a GlobalData report.The integration of credit cards with UPI is expected to increase utilisation, particularly in ecommerce and higher-value spending, while UPI-powered digital wallets continue to be widely used for day-to-day transactions. Credit cards also offer consumers rewards, discounts and instalment payment options, supporting their adoption. Advt India had 122.9 million outstanding credit cards as of July, compared with 1.03 billion debit cards, according to the latest Reserve Bank of India data. Debit cards remain the most widely held card type, supported by financial inclusion initiatives and the expansion of formal banking access.Credit and charge card adoption remains comparatively low because of limited formal credit histories, particularly in rural areas, as well as concerns over interest costs and debt. However, rising incomes, greater awareness and promotional campaigns by banks are supporting increased adoption.The integration with UPI could widen the range of transactions where credit cards can be used by enabling payments through UPI QR codes, including at merchants that do not accept cards through traditional point-of-sale infrastructure. This could make cards more relevant in areas where conventional card acceptance remains limited.Riding on e-commerceEcommerce expansion is also supporting wider adoption of electronic payments and is expected to contribute to card usage. Credit cards are likely to remain relevant for higher-value spending, where consumers can use credit while accessing rewards, discounts and instalment options.The expansion of formal financial services is creating a broader base for electronic payment adoption. More than 590 million accounts and over 410 million RuPay cards had been issued under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana as of August, highlighting the role of bundled debit cards in bringing first-time users into the formal financial system. Advt The Financial Inclusion Index rose to 70 as of March-end from 67 a year earlier, reflecting continued progress in access to financial services, financial literacy and consumer protection.Going ahead, credit card utilisation is expected to benefit from wider UPI integration, particularly as UPI provides a broader acceptance network for card-linked payments. Continued ecommerce expansion, rising incomes and greater adoption of credit products could further support card usage, according to the GlobalData report. rows.title: GDP growth debate: Is the deflator making India’s 7.8% growth look stronger?
rows.desc: Articles 7 min read GDP growth debate: Is the deflator making India’s 7.8% growth look stronger? Critics have questioned whether the combination of a new base year, changes in price measures and revisions to previous estimates has resulted in an unusually high real growth rate. ETBFSI Research ETBFSI Published On Sep 5, 2026 at 08:40 AM IST var news_msid = 133785757; console.log(news_msid); Select ETBFSI as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook India’s 7.8% real GDP growth in the April-June quarter has triggered a debate over the methodology behind the latest national accounts series, with questions focusing particularly on the GDP deflator and revisions to earlier estimates. The government has defended the numbers, saying the changes reflect the new 2022-23 base year, improved data sources and methodological changes rather than an attempt to inflate growth.Here is what the controversy is about and how the GDP deflator affects the growth calculation.What exactly is the controversy over the 7.8% GDP growth rate?India’s real GDP grew 7.8% year-on-year in Q1 FY27, compared with 6.9% a year earlier. Nominal GDP grew 10.3%, while real GVA grew 8.2%. The growth was stronger than the Reserve Bank of India’s earlier 7% forecast and market expectations of around 7.1%. Advt The controversy arose because the new GDP series has also significantly revised earlier data. Critics have questioned whether the combination of a new base year, changes in price measures and revisions to previous estimates has resulted in an unusually high real growth rate.The government has rejected that interpretation, saying the new series incorporates improved data sources and methodological changes in line with national accounting practices.What is the GDP deflator?The GDP deflator is the implicit price index obtained by comparing GDP at current prices with GDP at constant prices. It captures the price changes associated with the goods and services included in domestic output.In simple terms, it helps separate the change in the value of economic output into its price and volume components.For Q1 FY27, nominal GDP grew 10.3%, while real GDP grew 7.8%. The relationship between the two implies an increase of roughly 2.3% in the implicit GDP deflator.Why has the GDP deflator become central to the issue?Because the gap between nominal and real GDP growth is relatively small.A 10.3% increase in nominal GDP and 7.8% real growth implies an implicit GDP deflator increase of roughly 2.3%. Critics argue that if the relevant economy-wide price increase were higher, the resulting real GDP growth would be lower. Advt This is why the debate has focused on whether the price measures used in the new GDP series adequately capture price changes across the economy.However, it would be incorrect to conclude that a low GDP deflator automatically means real GDP growth is overstated. The deflator is derived from the prices and weights relevant to different components of national output. It is not simply another measure of CPI or WPI inflation.Why doesn’t the GDP deflator simply use CPI inflation?Because the GDP deflator and consumer price inflation measure different things.CPI measures changes in the prices of a basket of goods and services consumed by households. The GDP deflator captures price changes across the goods and services included in domestic output and also reflects changes in the composition of production. Advt WPI, meanwhile, measures wholesale prices of selected goods. Neither CPI nor WPI can therefore simply be substituted for the GDP deflator.The new national accounts series has introduced more granular price data and expanded the range of deflators used in the national accounts, including the use of producer price data in relevant areas.What has changed in the new GDP series?The latest national accounts series uses 2022-23 as the base year, replacing the earlier base year. MoSPI released the new series in February 2026.The latest estimates incorporate the new Output PPI, a revised Index of Industrial Production series with 2022-23 as its base and updated administrative data. MoSPI has also revised quarterly estimates from Q1 FY23 through Q4 FY26. Advt This means comparisons with older GDP estimates need to be made carefully because the underlying methodology and data sources have changed.What is “double deflation” and why is it being discussed?Double deflation is particularly important for manufacturing.Under the new methodology, MoSPI separately deflates output and intermediate consumption, rather than applying the same deflator to both. Real manufacturing GVA is then calculated as real output minus real intermediate consumption.The objective is to capture changes in both selling prices and input costs more accurately.For example, if manufacturers’ input costs rise faster than their output prices, their real value added can behave differently from their nominal valu

rows.title: AU SFB seen sustaining 20%+ credit growth as universal-bank transition advances
rows.desc: Articles 3 min read AU SFB seen sustaining 20%+ credit growth as universal-bank transition advances The bank's Rs 1.34 lakh crore loan book as of March 2026 would place it among the top-10 private sector banks following the transition, while its nearly 90% retail asset mix gives it a distinct positioning among large private lenders. ETBFSI Research ETBFSI Published On Sep 5, 2026 at 08:43 AM IST Read by 100 Professionals var news_msid = 133785840; console.log(news_msid); Select ETBFSI as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook AU Small Finance Bank is poised to sustain credit growth of more than 20% over FY26-FY28 as it transitions towards becoming a universal bank, potentially allowing it to continue gaining market share even as private sector lenders have lost momentum against public sector banks.The bank's Rs 1.34 lakh crore loan book as of March 2026 would place it among the top-10 private sector banks following the transition, while its nearly 90% retail asset mix gives it a distinct positioning among large private lenders. AU has also delivered more than 30% loan and profit CAGR over the past decade, with average credit costs of around 1% and RoE above 15%, according to a report by ICICI Securities. Advt The Reserve Bank of India had granted AU SFB in-principle approval to transition into a universal bank in August 2025. The move is expected to provide a platform for the lender to scale its franchise further as it seeks to gain both credit and deposit market share.AU's incremental credit market share stood at 1% in FY26, compared with 0.6% on a period-end basis, indicating that the lender has been growing faster than the system and gaining share from existing players. This comes at a time when private sector banks have seen their pace of market-share gains moderate, while public sector banks have captured a larger share of incremental credit.Selected private sector banks recorded average credit growth of about 14% between FY23 and FY26, compared with more than 20% during FY15-FY19. AU, in contrast, has maintained loan growth of more than 30% over the past decade, supported by its retail franchise, distribution network and underwriting capabilities in semi-urban and rural markets.Retail strengthRetail assets accounted for nearly 90% of AU's loan portfolio as of June 2026, one of the highest proportions among the top-10 private sector banks. Large private sector peers typically have retail asset shares of 50-75%, with unsecured loans accounting for around 10-20% of their portfolios. Advt AU has focused on expanding secured retail lending while keeping unsecured exposure below 15%. Despite its relatively lower unsecured loan share and higher cost of deposits, its net interest margin leads the pack among the top-10 private sector banks, the report said.The bank's growth has also been accompanied by contained credit costs. Its average credit cost over the past decade was around 1%, with a peak of 1.9% and a low of 0.3%. This has enabled AU to maintain a cross-cycle RoE of around 15% while delivering substantially higher loan growth than many private-sector peers.The lender is expected to benefit from further expansion of its retail distribution, including through Fincare touch points in south India. Growth could also be supported by a recovery in microfinance, credit cards and personal loans, along with stronger traction in gold loans from a relatively low base. Advt AU has simultaneously been strengthening its deposit franchise. Deposits grew 23% year-on-year in FY26, while CASA deposits increased 20%. Overall deposits expanded at a 34% CAGR between FY21 and FY26, helping reduce the premium AU pays over larger private sector banks for term deposits.AU's peak term-deposit rate premium over the top three private sector banks, which exceeded 100 basis points in FY23, had declined to 80 basis points by August 2026. Excluding the top three private banks, the premium had fallen to around 25 basis points, pointing to an improvement in its liability franchise.The share of CASA, retail term deposits and non-callable bulk term deposits increased to around 79% of deposits by June 2026 from about 65% in March 2024. More than 80% of AU's deposits are mobilised from urban markets, with Maharashtra accounting for 23%, Rajasthan 20% and Delhi 14% as of March 2026. Advt AU has more than 500 urban branches within its total network of 703 branches and plans to add 80-100 branches annually, with a focus on the top 20 cities that already account for around 57% of its deposits.The bank's deposit market share stood at 0.6% as of March 2026. While it has built a strong savings-account proposition through digital channels, developing a stronger current-account franchise remains a longer-term challenge as it seeks to deepen relationships with individual and retail customers. rows.title: FCNR inflows to dilute bank margins, but could add Rs 10,000 crore to bank earnings
rows.desc: Articles 4 min read FCNR inflows to dilute bank margins, but could add Rs 10,000 crore to bank earnings The record USD 127.2 billion FCNR-B mobilisation is set to reshape banks’ funding mix, with Jefferies expecting near term NIM compression but an annual Rs 10,000-11,000 crore addition to the banking sector’s profit pool. CareEdge, meanwhile, estimates core banking-system liquidity could swell to Rs 13-14 lakh crore by December, potentially accelerating the decline in wholesale funding costs. Shrishti Sharma ETBFSI Updated On Sep 4, 2026 at 06:19 PM IST Read by 100 Professionals var news_msid = 133763281; console.log(news_msid); Select ETBFSI as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook The record mobilisation of FCNR(B) deposits is likely to create a near term squeeze on banks’ net interest margins (NIMs), the scale of inflows which happened to be four times of 2013, could ultimately add around Rs 10,000-11,000 crore annually to the banking sector’s earnings, according to Jefferies.The brokerage estimates that FCNR-B deposits could create an additional profit pool of Rs 100-110 billion a year, equivalent to around 2 per cent of the banking sector’s profit before tax. While the deposits are structurally a lower-NIM business and are likely to dilute both NIM and return on assets (ROA), they are expected to be accretive to net interest income (NII) and return on equity (ROE). Advt The concessional swap window for FCNR-B deposits closed on August 31, with FCNR-B inflows reaching USD 127.2 billion. Including USD 5.3 billion raised through overseas foreign currency borrowings and USD 3.9 billion through ECBs, total inflows under the broader RBI scheme stood at USD 136.4 billion by August 31.Why NIMs could come under pressureThe first impact on bank margins is expected to be visible in the second quarter, according to Jefferies.Banks had raised bonds and loans ahead of receiving and deploying the FCNR-B deposits, creating a timing mismatch between the cost of funds and their deployment. As a result, the brokerage expects banks to report lower NIMs in Q2 and potentially quantify the short-term impact as a non-recurring effect.There is also a structural reason for the lower margin profile. FCNR-B deposits involve what Jefferies describes as a “double-counting” of deposits and assets, with the first leg of the transaction generating only a 10-15 basis point spread.This means that a sharp increase in FCNR-B balances can mechanically dilute the average margin even when the transaction adds to absolute interest income.“While FCNR-B deposits dilute NIMs & ROA, they are accretive to NII & ROE,” the brokerage said, estimating an annual Rs 100-110 billion addition to the sector’s earnings.Funding costThe larger opportunity for banks could come from how they use the new foreign-currency funding to change their existing liability and asset mix. Advt Jefferies expects banks to gradually normalise margins over the next two to four quarters by reducing their dependence on high-cost wholesale deposits, lowering the proportion of government securities held for liquidity coverage requirements and reducing exposure to low-margin overseas trade financing.This could create a second-order benefit for banks. If FCNR-B funds allow lenders to replace relatively expensive domestic wholesale deposits, the initial NIM dilution could be offset over time through a lower overall cost of funds.The early signs of this funding-cost reset are already visible in the money markets. Three-month certificate of deposit rates fell by 90 basis points in the last month to 5.9%, while six-month CD rates declined by 50 basis points to 6.46 per cent, according to Jefferies. Advt The brokerage expects banks to lower wholesale funding rates further as the liquidity impact of the FCNR-B inflows works through the system.Liquidity glut could amplify pressure on domestic ratesCareEdge's assessment suggests that the liquidity impact could be substantially larger than the immediate deposit numbers indicate.The rating agency estimates that core liquidity in the banking system, which stood at Rs 8.1 lakh crore in mid-August, could rise to around Rs 13-14 lakh crore by December-end in the absence of RBI liquidity-management operations. That would amount to around 4.5-5 per cent of net demand and time liabilities. Advt The calculation takes into account several offsets. CareEdge expects currency in circulation to rise by around Rs 1.1 lakh crore during the festive season, while the maturity of the RBI's short dollar-forward position could create another Rs 3 lakh crore drag on core liquidity. CRR accretion from deposit growth could absorb a further Rs 70,000 crore. Even after these adjustments, however, liquidity could still rise sharply.This creates the possibility of a broader funding-cost reset across the banking system.Jefferies estimates that system surplus liquidity has already risen to

rows.title: Niva Bupa hikes premiums 8-9% annually to keep pace with medical inflation: CFO Vishwanath Mahendra
rows.desc: Articles 7 min read Niva Bupa hikes premiums 8-9% annually to keep pace with medical inflation: CFO Vishwanath Mahendra Niva Bupa Health Insurance is prioritising profitable growth even as medical inflation continues to push up the cost of health cover, with the insurer raising premiums by around 8-9% annually and expecting this trend to continue. CFO Vishwanath Mahendra said smaller annual increases are preferable to sharp hikes every few years, while the insurer targets a 98-99% combined insurance service ratio by FY29 and mid-to-high teens ROE. Anushka Sengupta ETBFSI Published On Aug 29, 2026 at 08:08 AM IST Read by 100 Professionals var news_msid = 133602500; console.log(news_msid); Select ETBFSI as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Vishwanath Mahendra, CFO, Niva Bupa Health InsuranceNiva Bupa Health Insurance is seeing strong growth, with retail health premium rising 47% year-on-year in Q1, significantly ahead of the industry’s 32% growth. Overall premium grew 32%, while profit after tax nearly doubled 93% to Rs 138 crore, even as the insurer remained selective in group health amid an unfavourable pricing environment.But the growth is coming against a persistent challenge for the health insurance industry: rising medical inflation and the resulting pressure on premiums. Niva Bupa CFO Vishwanath Mahendra said the insurer has already raised premiums by 8-9% annually, and expects this to continue as medical costs rise, arguing that smaller, regular hikes are preferable to a sharp increase every few years. Advt Mahendra also said Niva Bupa is targeting profitable growth, with a medium-term goal of a 98-99% combined insurance service ratio by FY29 and mid-to-high teens ROE, while its retail market share has crossed 11%.Here are the edited excerpts from the interview:Q. By how much has Niva Bupa raised its premiums this year to tackle rising medical inflation. Should customers expect another round of hikes next year as well?Vishwanath: Medical inflation is something which is eating every day now. Ultimately, we have to pass on that to policyholders because there is no other way if we want to make the product sustainable in the long run.We have been increasing premiums in high single digits in the past, and we would like to continue doing that. Rather than increasing premiums once in three years by a big number, our preference is to increase them by only single digits every year, so that it is not as much of a pinch for policyholders.So, when I say 8-9%, I mean 8-9% per annum, which will be experienced by policyholders. And yes, this is something we expect to continue next year as well.Of course, we are also doing many other things, discussions with hospitals on treatment protocols, industry initiatives and care pathways, to ensure there are no unnecessary admissions, abuse or wastage. But at some point, inflation is there in the economy and we have to pass that on. Advt Q. Your retail health business grew 47% in Q1, much faster than the industry. Is that growth coming at healthy economics or are you sacrificing margins to gain market share?Vishwanath: It is coming from healthy economics. The growth is being driven by investment across distribution channels, product innovation and our claims practices.We have been investing across agency, bancassurance, direct-to-consumer and third-party channels. Our newly launched product, ReAssure 3.0, has also been received very well by distributors and customers.Our claim settlement ratio is close to 96%, and we are not compromising on underwriting or profitability to drive growth. Advt Q. You have also kept group health growth largely flat. Was that a conscious decision because pricing was not attractive?Vishwanath: Yes. We generally write business only if it is value-accretive. The pricing environment in group health was not very supportive, so we decided to stay away from business that was not economically attractive.We continue to focus on segments within group health which are good businesses from a profitability perspective. The approach is very clear, we want profitable growth, not growth at any cost.Q. With 32% overall growth and 93% growth in profit after tax, how close are you to consistently generating underwriting profits? Advt Vishwanath: We are very much there. It is only a matter of 20 basis points. Our combined insurance service ratio has improved by 300 basis points, from 103.2% to 100.2%.Our medium-term guidance since listing has been mid-to-high teens ROE, which corresponds to a 98-99% combined insurance service ratio by FY29. We are very much on that trajectory.Our post-tax ROE was 11.8% for the last four rolling quarters, so the trajectory is very much there.Q. Retail market share has crossed 11%. How much further do you want to take it?Vishwanath: Our target is to keep growing retail health at least 8-10% higher than the industry and keep gaining market share ever
rows.summary: Niva Bupa said it is raising health insurance premiums about 8-9% a year to offset medical inflation while focusing on profitable growth.

rows.title: RBI DG Murmu meets FIDC, NBFC CEOs; industry hopeful of partial ban on revolving credit
rows.desc: Articles 4 min read RBI DG Murmu meets FIDC, NBFC CEOs; industry hopeful of partial ban on revolving credit RBI DG S C Murmu recently held a meeting with NBFCs and the Finance Industry Development Council (FIDC), having already received 350 feedbacks from the industry on central bank's draft proposal of banning revolving credit. Exemption to Supply chain financing has garnered repeated attention during the discussion, with one of the senior industry participant saying final guidelines may come in another two months. Shrishti Sharma ETBFSI Updated On Sep 4, 2026 at 11:27 AM IST Read by 100 Professionals var news_msid = 133737739; console.log(news_msid); Select ETBFSI as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook The Reserve Bank of India may reconsider its proposed blanket ban on revolving credit facilities by non bank lenders after receiving feedback that the draft could affect a much wider section of the NBFC industry than initially envisaged, sources said.RBI Deputy Governor Shirish Chandra Murmu recently held a meeting with NBFCs and the Finance Industry Development Council (FIDC) to discuss the proposed restrictions on revolving credit, with the central bank listening to concerns raised by lenders, according to people aware of the discussions.The RBI had initially envisaged the impact of the proposed ban to be limited to around three to four NBFCs. However, feedback received during the consultation has indicated that a significantly larger section of the industry could be affected, prompting the central bank to consider whether a blanket prohibition is appropriate, sources said. Advt “Initially, the impact was seen as being limited to three or four NBFCs. But the feedback has shown that a much larger section of the industry could be impacted. RBI may therefore look at a partial restriction rather than a blanket ban,” an NBFC CEO said.The contours of any changes are yet to be finalised, the person added and all the suggestions discussed will be sent to RBI by Confederation of Indian Industry (CII).The development comes after substantial industry feedback on the draft. Around 30-40 lenders have submitted their responses to FIDC, while the RBI has received around 350 responses on the proposed revolving credit restrictions, according to sources.“RBI is still receiving a lot of views. The purpose of putting out a draft is to take the public view, absorb the feedback and then convert it into regulation,” another NBFC CEO said.The RBI's proposal had raised concerns across the NBFC industry over the scope of its definition of revolving credit and its potential impact on products and lending structures that are not necessarily intended to perpetually roll over credit.The central bank's concern behind the proposal is linked to the credibility and creditworthiness of borrowers, sources said. The proposed framework seeks to ensure greater discipline around the repayment and continuation of credit facilities rather than allowing credit limits to remain available on a revolving basis. Advt However, NBFCs have argued that there are several products where limited redraw or replenishment within an existing sanctioned facility does not necessarily amount to the kind of revolving lending that RBI is seeking to restrict.“The issue is that there is something in between a conventional term loan and what RBI may be defining as revolving credit. There are products that technically may not fit neatly into the definition, and that is where the industry has sought greater clarity,” an industry professional said.The industry has also pointed to the potential impact on working-capital and other lending products if the definition is applied too broadly. Advt “RBI has been quite positive in the discussions and is listening to the points being raised by the industry. That gives us confidence that the feedback will be considered before the final regulation,” an NBFC CEO said.The issue is not new, with NBFCs having raised concerns around the treatment of revolving credit with the RBI in earlier discussions as well. However, the latest draft has brought the issue into sharper focus by putting the proposed restrictions in writing.“There were discussions on the same issue even earlier, but there were no guidelines in writing. The moment something is put into a regulation, the grey areas become much more important because businesses have to comply with the exact wording,” an industry professional said. Advt The consultation process is therefore expected to play a key role in determining whether RBI retains the blanket restriction or introduces exemptions or a more targeted prohibition.Sources said the final guidelines could take another two months to be issued, giving the central bank time to assess the responses received from lenders and industry bodies.“The industry is not opposed to the objective of preventing evergreening or ensuring borrower credibility. rows.title: Ujjivan SFB leadership change puts Rs 1 lakh crore FY30 loan-book plan under watch
rows.desc: Articles 3 min read Ujjivan SFB leadership change puts Rs 1 lakh crore FY30 loan-book plan under watch Ujjivan SFB leadership change puts Rs 1 lakh crore FY30 loan-book plan under watchIntro: While the bank has reiterated that the early retirement of managing director and CEO Sanjeev Nautiyal will not affect its FY27 guidance or near-term strategic priorities, the eventual successor will be closely watched for continuity in executing the roadmap. ETBFSI Research ETBFSI Published On Sep 3, 2026 at 05:40 AM IST Read by 100 Professionals var news_msid = 133722599; console.log(news_msid); Select ETBFSI as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Ujjivan SFB targets a Rs 1 lakh crore loan book and 65-70% secured asset mix by FY30, with secured loans already rising to around 50%.The bank’s FY30 roadmap also targets CASA of 35%, deposits at three times Q1FY26 levels and 1,150 branches.Carol Furtado has taken interim charge as MD & CEO, while Ujjivan is expected to submit shortlisted candidates to the RBI within three to four months.Ujjivan has retained its FY27 guidance, with MSME growth and asset quality tracking broadly in line with expectations despite the leadership transition.Ujjivan Small Finance Bank’s strategy to scale its gross loan book to Rs 1 lakh crore and increase the share of secured assets to 65-70% by FY30 faces a leadership transition following the early retirement of managing director and CEO Sanjeev Nautiyal on health grounds. While the bank has reiterated that the change will not affect its FY27 guidance or near-term strategic priorities, the eventual successor will be closely watched for continuity in executing the roadmap.Nautiyal, who joined Ujjivan SFB in July 2024, played a key role in accelerating the bank’s diversification, with the secured share of the loan book rising from around 31% in June 2024 to around 50% in June 2026. The bank’s FY30 roadmap also envisages CASA of 35%, a deposit base three times the Q1FY26 level, a branch network of 1,150 and a reduction in the cost-to-income ratio to 55% and credit-to-assets ratio to below 5%, according to Axis Securities. Advt The bank is targeting a further increase in secured loans to 65-70% of the portfolio by FY30 as it moves towards a more diversified asset mix. The strategy also includes building the loan book to Rs 1 lakh crore, strengthening the liability franchise and expanding its digital and physical distribution network.The leadership change comes after Nautiyal sought early retirement citing health concerns. He ceased to hold the positions of MD & CEO and key managerial personnel with effect from September 1 and will remain on leave during his three-month notice period ending November 30. The bank has maintained that his early retirement is unrelated to its strategy, governance or operations.The interim CEOCarol Furtado, the bank’s existing executive director, has been appointed interim MD & CEO for three months, with the Reserve Bank of India approving the appointment. Furtado has more than three decades of banking experience across business, strategy, operations, people and institutional functions. She had also taken charge as Officer on Special Duty and subsequently as interim CEO during an earlier leadership transition at Ujjivan in 2021.Ujjivan is expected to begin the succession process ahead of the original November timeline and submit a list of shortlisted candidates to the RBI over the next three to four months. Both internal and external candidates will be considered, with Furtado remaining a potential internal candidate for the permanent MD & CEO position. Advt Despite the leadership change, the bank has maintained its FY27 guidance and indicated that its broader diversification strategy remains on track. The MSME business is tracking in line with FY27 guidance, while asset-quality outcomes have remained better than or broadly in line with Q1 performance, with no material deviations currently visible.The bank has also appointed Vikas Agarwal as head of its MSME business as it seeks to strengthen its leadership bandwidth. Agarwal has more than 25 years of experience across MSME, business banking, retail banking, credit, product and distribution.Ujjivan has remained non-committal on the timeline for reapplying for a universal bank licence, choosing instead to focus on its broader diversification strategy. The immediate priority is therefore execution of the existing business plan, including the shift towards secured lending, strengthening the deposit franchise and expanding MSME operations. Advt The key uncertainty for investors will be whether the eventual successor maintains the strategic direction established under Nautiyal. rows.title: September set for IPO boom as Jio, NSE could drive record fundraising
rows.desc: Articles 3 min read September set for IPO boom as Jio, NSE could drive record fundraising Jio's proposed Rs 37,700-crore issue has already received Sebi approval, while NSE's proposed Rs 30,000-crore issue could significantly add to September's fundraising if launched. ETBFSI Research ETBFSI Published On Sep 1, 2026 at 01:02 PM IST Read by 100 Professionals var news_msid = 133672651; console.log(news_msid); Select ETBFSI as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook JIO, NSE ఐపీఓలు.. ఇండియా స్టాక్ మార్కెట్ చరిత్ర తిరగరాయడం ఖాయమా?September’s IPO calendar has opened with mainboard issues from Purple Style Labs, Deepa Jewellers and Rays of Belief, alongside SME offerings.More than 25 companies are expected to tap the IPO market, with Zepto, PhonePe and Manipal Health among the larger names in the broader pipeline.Improved market sentiment and stronger listing gains have revived IPO activity after a subdued first half of CY26.Despite strong average IPO returns, wide variations in post-listing performance underline the need for selective stock picking.September could emerge as one of the biggest months for India’s primary market, with more than 25 companies expected to tap the IPO market and potential mega issues from Jio Platforms and the National Stock Exchange (NSE) capable of pushing monthly fundraising towards Rs 70,000 crore.The month has opened with a busy primary-market calendar. Purple Style Labs, Deepa Jewellers and Rays of Belief are among the mainboard offerings around the start of September, while Farm Peace, Phychem Technologies, Shanti Inorganics and Ashutosh Fibre are among the SME issues. The seven issues identified in the opening-week calendar together are looking to raise more than Rs 1,400 crore. Advt The biggest potential trigger, however, is Jio Platforms. The company has received Sebi approval for a proposed IPO of around Rs 37,700 crore, which would make it India's largest IPO if launched at that size. NSE is also considering a public issue of around Rs 30,000 crore, although its launch timing has not been confirmed.If either of the two mega issues comes to market in September, fundraising could rise sharply, with the month's total potentially approaching Rs 70,000 crore depending on the issue launched, its final size and the broader IPO pipeline.The possibility of a record September comes after a sharp revival in primary-market activity in July and August. Companies raised more than Rs 28,000 crore through IPOs in July, while 22 companies raised over Rs 23,000 crore in August. The August fundraising was the highest in a year in terms of the number of companies accessing the market.The revival follows a subdued first half of CY26, when market volatility, valuation concerns, foreign investor outflows and geopolitical tensions weighed on IPO activity. The Nifty 50 fell around 9% during H1 CY26, prompting several companies to defer their fundraising plans.Primary market boomMarket conditions improved in July and August, helping restore investor appetite. The Nifty 50 gained around 1.8% from the end of June through the first two months of the second half, while IPO listing performance improved substantially.The average listing-day gain of 25 IPOs that debuted between July 1 and August 19 stood at 20.9%, compared with 1.72% in H1 CY26. Across 47 mainboard IPOs during the year, the average listing gain was 11.9%. Advt The stronger listing performance has provided a more favourable backdrop for September's IPO pipeline. Companies that had held back their plans amid weaker market conditions now have greater incentive to proceed, while merchant bankers have a sizeable pool of approved and filed offerings to bring to market.The broader pipeline includes large companies such as Zepto, PhonePe and Manipal Health, among others. However, these companies should not be treated as confirmed September IPOs, as their launch dates have not been announced.The pipeline remains sizeable. Since March 2025, 146 companies have received Sebi approval, while 67 are awaiting regulatory approval, 65 have filed DRHPs and another 33 have filed confidential DRHPs. This gives the primary market a substantial pool of potential issuers beyond the current September calendar. Advt The surge in IPO activity will nevertheless test the market's ability to absorb a large supply of new equity. Large offerings from Jio Platforms and potentially NSE could compete for institutional and retail liquidity with smaller mainboard and SME issues coming to market at the same time.Investor returns also remain uneven despite the improvement in sentiment. The average gain from issue price across 407 IPOs stood at 66% as of July 31, but 17% of companies were trading 25-50% below their issue price and another 9% were more than 50% below the issue price. By ETBFSI Research , ETBFSI Published On Sep 1, 2026 at 01:02 PM IST Telegram Facebook Copy Link Comments What are you
rows.summary: India’s IPO market may see record September fundraising, led by potential large issues from Jio Platforms and NSE amid stronger investor sentiment.
