rows.title: Circular for Seeking comments on XBRL for Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process
rows.summary:
This circular, issued by the National Stock Exchange of India on June 21, 2023, is a request for comments from all listed companies and their Company Secretaries/Resolution Professionals on a proposed migration of Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) announcements from PDF to XBRL format. The stated objective is to standardize and streamline disclosure data for CIRP-related announcements under the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 and related SEBI provisions by moving these filings to XBRL exclusively, with the draft format attached as an annexure for feedback on the fields and structure. The exchange explains that it has already been progressively shifting compliance filings from PDF to XBRL, and that this proposal would make CIRP disclosures subject to the same machine-readable reporting approach.

For compliance purposes, the key immediate requirement is not yet a filing mandate, but a consultation response: listed entities may submit suggestions, comments, additions, or modifications to the proposed XBRL fields by email to DL-Announcement@nse.co.in, using the subject line “Comments / Feedback on the XBRL being introduced for CIRP.” The deadline for sending comments is June 25, 2023. The circular provides a detailed draft XBRL schema for CIRP announcements, indicating which fields are mandatory versus non-mandatory and the information expected to be captured, including NSE symbol, company name, BSE scrip code, MSE symbol, ISIN, type of announcement (new/update/revised), type of event, dates of initial/latest/original announcement, and report date.

The draft CIRP event taxonomy is broad and covers multiple stages of the insolvency process: application filed by the company or financial creditors, initiation of CIRP pursuant to an NCLT order, rejection/withdrawal/stay of the application, appointment or replacement of the resolution professional, prior or post-facto intimation of Committee of Creditors meetings, number of resolution plans received, filing of a resolution plan with the tribunal, prior intimation of NCLT consideration of a resolution plan, approval or rejection by the tribunal, liquidation, and an “others” category. For the company-filed CIRP case, the draft also requires the date of the board meeting approving the CIRP event, reasons for opting for CIRP, whether shareholders approved it, the date of the shareholders’ meeting, reasons if shareholder approval was not obtained, details of default in financial obligations as of the date in INR lakhs, whether the default had already been intimated to the exchange under the November 21, 2019 SEBI circular, and the date of the initial default disclosure. The circular also distinguishes between fields intended for public website dissemination and those for exchange-only use, such as certain remarks fields, showing that the proposed XBRL format will require more structured, standardized data capture than current PDF-based narrative filings.

rows.title: Circular for Seeking of comments, feedback on the XBRL for Loss of Share Certificate/Issue of Duplicate Share Certificate and Closure of Trading Window
rows.summary:
This circular is a consultation notice from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited dated June 14, 2023, asking listed entities to comment on a proposal to move certain corporate announcements from PDF submission to mandatory XBRL-only submission. The two announcement categories covered are: (1) loss of share certificate / issue of duplicate share certificate, and (2) closure of trading window, both under SEBI LODR and/or SEBI PIT requirements and any related SEBI law, regulation, circular, or provision. NSE explains that the purpose of the change is to standardize securities market data, reduce compliance burden through a uniform data structure, and improve analysis of disclosures; it also notes that XBRL filings for financials have already been mandated since 2015 and that exchanges have been progressively converting other disclosures from PDF to XBRL.

For the loss/duplicate share certificate item, the draft XBRL format requires very specific data fields, including NSE symbol, company name, BSE scrip code, MSE symbol, ISIN, announcement type (new or revision), event type (loss of share certificates, issue of duplicate share certificates, or “others”), date of original announcement, website remarks, exchange-only remarks, and date of report. It also requires transaction-level details such as the date the company received intimation/information of the lost certificate, shareholder name(s) including joint holders, folio number, number of shares, certificate number, and distinctive number ranges, plus an indication of whether multiple entries must be created for one shareholder and how many entries are needed for that shareholder. The draft further requires identification of the company’s registrar and transfer agent, with a field to specify the name if “Others” is selected, and compliance confirmations on whether the company has complied with Rule 19(3) of the Securities Contract (Regulations) Rules, 1957 and Regulation 39(2) of SEBI LODR; if not compliant, the company must state the reason. The annexure also shows that the loss-of-certificate data structure contemplates add/delete row functionality and a field for the number of shareholders who have reported loss of share certificates.

NSE is specifically soliciting comments, feedback, suggestions, and observations on additions or modifications to the fields in the draft XBRL format, recognizing that the required information is largely descriptive and derived from the existing SEBI framework. Comments must be emailed to DL-Announcement@nse.co.in in a prescribed format that includes the name of the entity/person, contact number and email address, the event category, the subject/heading/field being commented on, comments/suggestions, and detailed rationale. The email subject must read exactly: “Comments / Feedback on the XBRL being introduced for Loss of Share Certificate/ Issue of Duplicate Share Certificate and Closure of Trading Window.” The deadline for submissions is June 20, 2023. The circular does not itself impose the final migration yet; it is a consultation on the draft format, but it clearly signals that listed entities should prepare for exclusive XBRL filing of these announcement types once the format is finalized.

rows.title: Filing of Annual Secretarial Compliance Report (ASCR) in XBRL format on NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform
rows.summary:
This circular informs all listed entities that the National Stock Exchange will make the facility for filing the Annual Secretarial Compliance Report (ASCR) under Regulation 24A of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 available in XBRL mode on the NEAPS platform starting **June 15, 2023**. It is a new filing channel, not a change to the underlying ASCR obligation itself, but it adds a specific technical submission requirement for entities filing through the Exchange.

The circular also sets the filing deadline for the **Secretarial Compliance Report for Financial Year ending March 31, 2023** as **June 30, 2023**. Listed entities subject to Regulation 24A must use the NEAPS workflow to submit the report in XBRL format: log in to the NEAPS portal, navigate to **COMPLIANCE > Common XBRL Upload**, choose **Secretarial Compliance Report** from the Module dropdown, download the offline Excel utility provided for that subject, complete it and generate the XML file, then enter the required portal details, attach the SCR in **PDF** form, and click **“Upload XBRL File”** to finish submission.

The document therefore affects **all listed entities** required to file the ASCR/SCR under SEBI LODR. It does not specify any new numerical thresholds or filing fee changes, but it does impose a specific submission method and sequence for the XBRL filing. For questions, the Exchange directs filers to the Secretarial Compliance team at **nsexbrl@nse.co.in** or via **NEAPS > Help > Contact Us**.

rows.title: Online processing of investor service requests and complaints by RTAs
rows.summary: This NSE circular is a transmittal notice to all listed companies informing them of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/72 dated June 8, 2023, titled “Online processing of investor service requests and complaints by RTAs.” The NSE circular itself does not set out detailed substantive requirements or new thresholds; it advises that the SEBI circular is enclosed and should be reviewed for necessary action, and notes that the circular is also available on the NSE website. It is addressed to the Company Secretary of all listed companies, so the compliance impact is on listed entities, but the actual operational obligations are contained in the underlying SEBI circular rather than in this NSE covering communication. The document does not specify any effective date beyond the June 8, 2023 issuance date, nor does it mention any numbers, rates, deadlines, or procedural steps in the text provided.

rows.title: Model Tripartite Agreement between the Issuer Company, Existing Share Transfer Agent and New Share Transfer Agent as per Regulation 7(4) of SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulation, 2015
rows.summary:
The notice is a transmittal circular from the National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. (NSE) dated May 26, 2023, addressed to the Company Secretary of all listed companies, informing them of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/79 dated May 25, 2023. The SEBI circular is titled “Model Tripartite Agreement between the Issuer Company, Existing Share Transfer Agent and New Share Transfer Agent as per Regulation 7(4) of SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulation, 2015,” which indicates that SEBI has issued a model agreement to be used when an issuer company changes its share transfer agent.  

For compliance purposes, the key substantive point is that the tripartite agreement is intended to be entered into among three parties: the listed issuer company, the existing share transfer agent, and the new share transfer agent, in connection with Regulation 7(4) of the SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015. The document excerpt provided does not state any numerical threshold, filing deadline, implementation date beyond the circular dates themselves, or specific operational step-by-step requirements; it simply forwards SEBI’s circular and advises listed companies to take “necessary action” at their end. The NSE also notes that the SEBI circular is enclosed and available on the NSE website for reference, implying that companies undergoing a share transfer agent transition should review the SEBI-issued model agreement and align their transition documentation and arrangements accordingly.

rows.title: Dematerialization of securities of Hold Cos and SPVs held by Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs)
rows.summary: The National Stock Exchange of India issued this circular on May 23, 2023, to all listed Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) and all parties to REITs and InvITs, drawing attention to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2023/76 dated May 22, 2023 on the “Dematerialization of securities of Hold Cos and SPVs held by Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs).” The NSE circular itself does not set out the substantive requirements in detail; rather, it forwards SEBI’s circular and instructs recipients to review it and take necessary action. The only concrete operational point in this document is that the SEBI circular is enclosed and also available on the NSE website for reference. For compliance purposes, this means any listed InvIT and relevant REIT/InvIT participants should immediately assess the SEBI circular’s requirements regarding dematerializing securities of holding companies and special purpose vehicles, since this NSE communication indicates the rule has been formally issued and action may be required, but it does not specify implementation dates, thresholds, or procedures on its own.

rows.title: Dematerialization of securities of Hold Cos and SPVs held by Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs)
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) has circulated SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2023/75 dated May 22, 2023, titled “Dematerialization of securities of Hold Cos and SPVs held by Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs).” The NSE’s own circular is Ref. No. NSE/CML/2023/35 dated May 23, 2023 and is addressed to the Company Secretary of all listed REITs and all parties to REITs and InvITs. This NSE communication does not itself set out the detailed compliance requirements; it serves to inform recipients that SEBI has issued the referenced circular, encloses it for necessary action, and notes that the circular is also available on the NSE website.

For compliance purposes, the material point in this document is that SEBI has issued a new regulatory circular specifically on the dematerialization of securities of holding companies (Hold Cos) and special purpose vehicles (SPVs) held by REITs, which implies affected REITs and their related parties must review SEBI’s May 22, 2023 instructions and implement any required actions relating to demat form/processing for those securities. No deadline, implementation date, threshold, rate, or procedural detail is stated in the NSE covering letter itself, so the operative compliance obligations must be taken from the enclosed SEBI circular rather than this brief NSE notice.

rows.title: FAQ’s on filing of announcements in XBRL format on NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform.
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated May 15, 2023 (Ref. NSE/CML/2023/34) provides FAQs on the use of XBRL format for filing certain equity-related announcements on the NEAPS platform, following the earlier circular NSE/CML/2023/28 dated March 31, 2023. It applies to all listed companies and clarifies that the Exchange is asking companies to file **both** a PDF disclosure and an XBRL submission for the covered subjects during the current transition period; the Exchange will later issue a separate circular stating the effective date after which XBRL will become the operative compliance filing.  

For now, the compliance timeline is that the **XBRL filing must be submitted within 24 hours of the PDF disclosure**, but the **PDF submission is currently the one counted for compliance purposes**. NSE specifically states that this will change only after a further circular, at which point only XBRL submissions will be treated as compliance. Companies with questions are directed to the NSE Announcements team at **takeover@nse.co.in** or the NEAPS contact details.  

The FAQ confirms the XBRL requirement covers the Regulation 30 disclosures listed in the circular, including: issuance or forfeiture of securities; split or consolidation of shares; buyback of securities; restrictions on transferability of securities; and alterations in the terms or structure of existing securities, including forfeiture, reissue of forfeited securities, alteration of calls, and redemption of securities. It also covers binding agreements not in the ordinary course of business, including shareholder agreements, JV agreements, family settlement agreements that affect management and control of the listed entity, and agreements/treaties/contracts with media companies, along with any revisions, amendments, or terminations of those agreements. In addition, it covers fraud/defaults by a promoter, key managerial personnel, or the listed entity itself; arrest of a promoter or KMP; one-time settlements with banks; resolution plans or restructuring relating to bank/financial institution borrowings including inter-creditor arrangements and corporate debt restructuring; and notices of shareholders’ meetings.  

The document further breaks down the covered securities-related events into NEAPS XBRL utility categories, including “Issuance/Allotment/Alteration/Restriction on transferability of securities,” with sub-coverage for issuance of securities under point 2.1 of the September 9, 2015 Continuous Disclosure Requirements Circular, alteration of capital under point 2.2, actions resulting in alteration of the terms or structure of existing securities under point 2.5, restrictions on transferability under point 2.4, and allotment of securities after issuance. The allotment category explicitly includes allotments of equity, preference, convertible, non-convertible, ESOP/ESPS, or other securities, and the FAQ notes that companies may be asked to provide details such as the board meeting date approving the issuance and whether any prior disclosure was made regarding the issuance.

rows.title: Introduction of Issue Summary Document (ISD) – Buy-back
rows.summary:
This circular from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE) informs all listed companies that, pursuant to SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/29 dated February 15, 2023, a new **Issue Summary Document (ISD)** filing requirement has been introduced for certain buy-back transactions. The requirement applies to **buy-back of equity shares through tender offer** and **buy-back of equity shares from the open market**, and the ISD must be filed in **XBRL format**. The new SEBI requirement is effective **May 2, 2023**.

For compliance purposes, NSE has enabled the necessary filing utilities on the **NEAPS** platform to support submission of the ISD in the prescribed format. Listed entities must log in to the NEAPS portal at **https://neaps.nseindia.com/NEWLISTINGCORP**, go to **COMPLIANCE >> Common XBRL Upload**, select **“Issue Summary Document (ISD) for Buyback”** from the Module tab, then choose the relevant announcement subject, download the applicable offline Excel XBRL utility, complete it, generate the XML file, and finally upload the XML along with the required portal details through **Upload XBRL File**.

The circular does not specify any quantitative thresholds, fees, or exemption criteria; the key compliance change is the addition of a formal XBRL-based ISD filing workflow for buy-back events. Companies undertaking covered buy-back transactions after the effective date must use this process to ensure their disclosures are submitted correctly. For questions, NSE directs users to the **Announcements team at takeover@nse.co.in** or to the contact details available on the NEAPS platform.

rows.title: FAQs on the submission of the quarterly Corporate Governance Report.
rows.summary:
This circular from the National Stock Exchange of India dated April 10, 2023 is a guidance-only FAQ document for listed entities filing the quarterly Corporate Governance Report on the NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) / data entry / XBRL utility. It does not amend law, SEBI regulations, or prior exchange circulars, but it does set out the Exchange’s required approach for completing specific fields in the submission, and listed entities are instructed to follow it accordingly.

For the Board composition section, if a director does not have a DIN or PAN, the company must enter the prescribed dummy values only — DIN `99999999` and PAN `ZZZZZ9999Z` — and explain the reason in the company remarks. The report must show the director’s correct and complete name as per PAN; if the name or PAN is inconsistent, the Exchange may seek clarification or issue an advisory letter. For chairperson classification, where the chairperson is the promoter or is related to the promoter and is also an Executive Director or Non-Executive Director, the company must select Code `C` together with Code `ED/NED`; where the chairperson is not related to promoters and is also an Executive Director or Non-Executive Director, the company must select Code `C` and Code `ED/NED` as well.

The circular also standardizes how appointment and re-appointment dates are to be entered. For Independent Directors, the initial appointment date is the start of the first term after the Companies Act, 2013 took effect, and the re-appointment date is the start of the second term; the FAQ gives the example that if a person served from 2011, was treated as an Independent Director from 2014, and was re-appointed in 2019, then 2014 is the initial appointment date and 2019 is the re-appointment date. For directors other than Independent Directors, the initial appointment date is the original date they were inducted onto the board, and re-appointment means the date of the current term.

The re-appointment field is mandatory for Independent Directors; if the first term is still continuing and the director has not yet been re-appointed, the company must repeat the initial appointment date in the re-appointment field. The cessation date field is mandatory only when the director’s tenure has ended because of death, resignation, removal, or completion of term, and if a director has died, the reason must be stated in the remarks column. Tenure details are mandatory only for Independent Directors, and the tenure is to be computed up to the end of the current/approved term as applicable.

rows.title: Introduction of Issue Summary Document (ISD) – Further Issues.
rows.summary:

Once I have readable content, I can produce the detailed compliance summary you requested, including:

rows.title: Additional affirmations by Practicing Company Secretaries (PCS) in Annual Secretarial Compliance Report (ASCR)
rows.summary:
The NSE’s April 10, 2023 circular revises the Annual Secretarial Compliance Report (ASCR) format for all listed entities by replacing item 1 in the earlier March 16, 2023 circular and adding a new set of mandatory affirmations to be made by the Practicing Company Secretary (PCS). The revised ASCR now requires the PCS to specifically state whether the listed entity complies with applicable Secretarial Standards issued by the ICSI, whether all applicable SEBI-regulatory policies have been adopted with board approval and are kept aligned with SEBI regulations/circulars/guidelines through timely review and updating, whether the company maintains a functional website and timely posts required information in a separate section, and whether web-links cited in the annual corporate governance report under Regulation 27(2) are accurate and directly point to the relevant document or section. It also requires affirmations that none of the company’s directors are disqualified under Section 164 of the Companies Act, 2013; that the listed entity has properly identified material subsidiaries and complied with disclosure requirements for both material and other subsidiaries; that records are preserved and destroyed in accordance with SEBI-prescribed record retention and archival policies under the SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015; that board, independent director, and committee performance evaluations have been carried out at the start of every financial year as required; that all related party transactions received prior Audit Committee approval or, if not, are fully explained and identified as later approved/ratified/rejected; that all Regulation 30 and Schedule III disclosures have been made within the prescribed timelines; and that the entity complies with Regulation 3(5) and 3(6) of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. The PCS must also state whether any action has been taken by SEBI or any stock exchange against the listed entity, its promoters, directors, or subsidiaries, including actions under SEBI’s SOP frameworks, and whether any additional non-compliances have been observed under any SEBI regulation, circular, or guidance note; if any item is marked “No” or “NA,” PCS remarks are mandatory.  

In addition, the circular changes the filing procedure temporarily: although listed entities are currently submitting ASCR in both PDF and XBRL, the XBRL filing mode is still under development, so ASCR must provisionally be submitted in PDF format through the NEAPS announcement path (NEAPS > Compliance > Announcements > Announcements/Corporate Actions Later). NSE states that once the XBRL system is ready, submission in XBRL will also become mandatory. The circular says the rest of the March 16, 2023 requirements remain unchanged, and the revised ASCR format is attached as Annexure A.

rows.title: Comprehensive FAQs on SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is a transmittal notice, not a standalone rule change. On April 5, 2023, the National Stock Exchange of India informed members that SEBI had issued “Comprehensive FAQs on SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015” on March 31, 2023, and provided the web link to SEBI’s clarification page, noting that the document was also enclosed and available on the NSE website.

For compliance teams, the practical significance is that the operative content comes from SEBI’s March 31, 2023 FAQs, which are intended to clarify how the SEBI PIT Regulations, 2015 should be interpreted and implemented. This circular itself does not impose a new deadline, threshold, rate, filing requirement, or amended obligation; it simply alerts members to the availability of SEBI’s clarifications and directs them to the official source. The affected audience is NSE members and, by extension, listed entities and other market participants subject to SEBI’s insider trading regime. A compliance officer should therefore review the referenced SEBI FAQs directly to determine whether any existing insider trading controls, trading window procedures, disclosures, code of conduct requirements, or monitoring practices need to be updated in light of SEBI’s interpretations.

rows.title: Filing of equity announcements in XBRL format on NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform.
rows.summary:
The NSE has expanded the use of XBRL for certain equity-related corporate announcements filed by listed companies on the NEAPS platform. Effective **April 1, 2023**, the following **Regulation 30, SEBI LODR** announcement categories must be made available in **XBRL format**: disclosures relating to issuance or forfeiture of securities, split or consolidation of shares, buyback of securities, restrictions on transferability or changes in the terms/structure of existing securities (including forfeiture, reissue of forfeited securities, alteration of calls, redemption, etc.); binding agreements not in the ordinary course of business (including shareholder agreements, JV agreements, family settlement agreements to the extent they affect management/control, and agreements/treaties/contracts with media companies), including amendments and terminations; fraud/defaults by a promoter, KMP, or the listed entity, or arrest of a promoter/KMP; one-time settlements with banks; resolution plans/restructuring for bank or financial institution borrowings (including inter-creditor arrangements); corporate debt restructuring; and notices of shareholders’ meetings.

For the initial phase, the NSE will still accept the **PDF filing** as compliance with Regulation 30, but listed entities must also file the **XBRL version within 24 hours of the PDF submission**. The circular states that at a later date—**to be announced separately**—the Exchange will move to **XBRL-only submission** for these subjects, so companies should treat the XBRL workflow as mandatory and prepare for a future hard transition away from PDF support.

The filing process must be done through the **NEAPS portal** at **https://neaps.nseindia.com/NEWLISTINGCORP** by navigating to **COMPLIANCE → Common XBRL Upload → Equity Announcement-XBRL**, selecting the relevant announcement subject, downloading the appropriate offline Excel utility, completing it to generate an XML file, and then uploading that XML file on the portal along with the required details. If companies have questions, they are directed to contact the NSE Announcements team at **takeover@nse.co.in** or use the contact details available on NEAPS.

rows.title: Extension of compliance period – Fund raising by large corporates through issuance of debt securities to the extent of 25% of their incremental borrowings in a financial year
rows.summary:
This NSE circular merely forwards and references SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHSRACPOD1/P/CIR/2023/049 dated March 31, 2023, and states that it is being issued for information and necessary action by listed companies. The subject of the SEBI circular is an **extension of the compliance period** for the requirement applicable to **large corporates** to **raise funds through issuance of debt securities to the extent of 25% of their incremental borrowings in a financial year**. The document itself does not set out the new extended deadline or the detailed mechanics; it directs recipients to the attached SEBI circular and to the NSE website for the operative text.

From a compliance perspective, the key point is that this is **not a new substantive funding obligation**, but an **extension of time to comply** with an existing framework concerning debt fundraising by large corporates. The affected entities are **listed companies** that fall within the SEBI definition of **large corporates** under the incremental borrowing/debt issuance regime. Compliance officers should review the underlying SEBI circular to confirm the revised compliance period, any reporting or disclosure deadlines, and whether any internal financing plans or debt issuance schedules need to be updated to align with the extended timeline.

rows.title: Introduction of Issue Summary Document (ISD) – Further Issues
rows.summary:
This NSE circular requires listed entities to begin filing a new Issue Summary Document (ISD) in XBRL format for specified “Further Issues,” pursuant to SEBI circular SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/29 dated February 15, 2023. The ISD requirement applies to preferential issues, qualified institutions placements (QIP), rights issues, issuances of American Depository Receipts (ADR), Global Depository Receipts (GDR), and Foreign Currency Convertible Bonds (FCCBs), with the new framework effective from April 3, 2023. NSE notes that stock exchanges have developed a utility to support filing, and the filing utility/instructions are provided in Annexure A, with NSE-specific submission procedure set out in Annexure B.

For compliance purposes, submission of ISD details is mandatory for any application filed on or after April 3, 2023 that seeks either: (i) in-principle approval under Regulation 28(1) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, or (ii) in-principle listing approval after allotment of securities. The listed entity must submit the ISD details to any stock exchange where the relevant securities are listed; if submitting to NSE, the filing must follow the method prescribed in Annexure B. The circular warns that failure to follow these directions will be treated as non-compliance and the corresponding application may not be approved.

rows.title: Standard Operating Process under SEBI(PIT) Regulations, 2015 for ensuring compliance with Structured Digital Database (“SDD”)
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated March 29, 2023 reiterates and continues the requirement for listed entities that are **not subject to Regulation 24A of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015** to maintain compliance with the **Structured Digital Database (SDD)** requirements under **SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015**. The key instruction is that such listed entities must **continue to submit the SDD Compliance Certificate on a quarterly basis**.

The filing deadline is **within 21 days from the end of each quarter**, and the certificate must be submitted by email to **sdd_pit@nse.co.in**. The circular expressly states that it is in continuation of prior NSE circulars dated **November 4, 2022**, **January 25, 2023**, and **March 16, 2023**, indicating that this is a continuing compliance obligation rather than a new substantive rule change.

The circular applies to **all listed entities**, but the specific quarterly certificate requirement is directed at those for whom **Regulation 24A of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 is not applicable**. The circular is **effective immediately**, so compliance teams should ensure ongoing quarterly tracking and timely submission without waiting for any further implementation date.

rows.title: Review of Securities available for trading under “permitted to trade” category
rows.summary:
This circular announces that the National Stock Exchange of India Limited is reviewing securities currently admitted for trading under the “permitted to trade” category. It explains that trading in securities under this category is allowed under Chapter IV-2(c) of the Byelaws and Regulation 3.1.1 of Part A of the Capital Market Segment, and that NSE has been admitting companies for dealings on this basis. The Exchange also notes that, under Chapter IV, Section 12 of the Byelaws and Regulation 3.1.2, it may prohibit dealings in any security and may suspend trading in particular securities at any time, in whatever manner and subject to whatever conditions it prescribes.

The circular highlights a key compliance distinction: companies admitted under “permitted to trade” do not execute the exchange listing agreement and therefore do not provide the full set of disclosures expected of listed entities. Because of stakeholder feedback, NSE is now reviewing the continued use of this category in consultation with, and on the advice of, the Exchange’s Relevant Authority. The document does not itself set a final removal list or immediate trading restriction; instead, it says the authority’s decisions will be communicated to market participants and that adequate notice will be given before any scrip is withdrawn from the “permitted to trade” category.

For compliance teams, the practical point is to monitor whether any securities in this category are subject to withdrawal following the review, and to prepare for a potential change in trading status only after NSE issues formal notice. The circular is dated March 29, 2023 and is addressed to all members and all permitted-to-trade companies.

rows.title: Common and simplified norms for processing investor’s service requests by RTAs and norms for furnishing PAN, KYC details and Nomination
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is a forwarding notice to all listed companies about a SEBI circular dated 16 March 2023 titled “Common and simplified norms for processing investor’s service requests by RTAs and norms for furnishing PAN, KYC details and Nomination.” NSE’s own communication is dated 22 March 2023 and does not itself introduce substantive requirements; it advises that the SEBI circular is enclosed and should be acted on as necessary.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the subject matter concerns how registrars and transfer agents (RTAs) must process investor service requests, and the norms applicable to furnishing PAN, KYC details, and nomination information. The NSE notice does not reproduce the operative SEBI requirements, deadlines, thresholds, or procedural steps in the text provided, so the underlying obligations would need to be taken directly from the SEBI circular referenced above. The notice indicates that the SEBI circular is available through NSE and is intended for information and necessary action by listed companies, implying that issuer-side coordination with RTAs and investor-facing compliance processes may be affected.

Because this NSE document is only a cover communication, it does not specify any separate effective date, grace period, reporting timeline, or numerical thresholds of its own beyond the SEBI circular’s date of 16 March 2023. A compliance team should treat this as a prompt to review the SEBI circular in full and confirm any changes required in issuer/RTA workflows relating to PAN, KYC, and nomination documentation for shareholders.

rows.title: Path of filing of disclosures related to Corporate Action on NEAPS Portal
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) has clarified the required filing path for corporate action disclosures on the NEAPS portal, applicable to all listed companies. Under Regulation 10 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, listed entities must file reports, statements, documents, filings, and other information on the Exchange’s specified electronic platform, and NSE has designated NEAPS for this purpose. The circular states that companies have been incorrectly uploading Record Date or Book Closure Date disclosures for corporate actions such as dividends and annual general meetings within other announcement categories, such as “Outcome of Board/Shareholder Meeting,” and instructs that these intimation(s) must instead be filed separately.

For compliance, all notices fixing a Record Date or Book Closure Date for any corporate action must be submitted through the dedicated NEAPS path: **NEAPS – Compliance – Announcements – Announcements/CA – Intimation Type: Corporate Action**. NSE specifically says it will recognize only disclosures filed under the relevant prescribed path and will take cognizance only of those submissions made through NEAPS in the correct category. The circular emphasizes that separate filing is required under **Regulation 42** for Record Date/Book Closure Date intimation, and failure to do so may result in the Exchange not taking the filing on record, with the listed entity bearing any resulting consequences.

There is no new numerical threshold, rate, or fixed deadline date in the circular; the requirement is immediate and procedural, and it applies to any listed entity making a corporate action disclosure involving Record Date or Book Closure Date. Compliance teams should ensure internal filing controls direct these disclosures to the standalone Corporate Actions tab rather than embedding them in general announcement filings.

rows.title: Additional affirmations by Practicing Company Secretaries (PCS) in Annual Secretarial Compliance Report (ASCR)
rows.summary:
NSE’s March 16, 2023 circular (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2023/21) requires all listed entities to use a revised Annual Secretarial Compliance Report (ASCR) format that adds several mandatory affirmations by the Practicing Company Secretary (PCS). The original ASCR framework was introduced by SEBI’s February 8, 2019 circular and has been applicable since March 31, 2019; the report remains an annual filing and is used to confirm compliance with SEBI regulations, circulars, and guidelines for listed entities and their material subsidiaries.

The circular expands the PCS’s scope of verification by requiring explicit confirmation on 12 areas: compliance with ICSI Auditing Standards CSAS-1 to CSAS-3; adoption, board approval, and timely updating of all applicable SEBI policies; maintenance of a functional website and timely uploading of required documents/information, including accurate and specific web-links in Regulation 27(2) corporate governance reports; confirmation that none of the company’s directors are disqualified under Section 164 of the Companies Act, 2013; identification and disclosure compliance for material and other subsidiaries; preservation and archival of records as required under SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015; performance evaluation of the Board, Independent Directors, and committees at the start of every financial year; prior Audit Committee approval for all related party transactions, or else detailed reasons plus whether later approved/ratified/rejected; timely disclosure of Regulation 30/Schedule III events and information; compliance with PIT Regulations 3(5) and 3(6); confirmation that neither SEBI nor stock exchanges have taken action against the listed entity, its promoters, directors, or subsidiaries (including under SEBI’s SOPs); and confirmation that no additional SEBI-related non-compliances were observed.

The revised ASCR format also adds two new disclosure tables that must be completed when there are exceptions or follow-up actions. The first table is for cases where the listed entity has not complied with a requirement; it requires the compliance requirement, regulation/circular number, nature of deviation, action taken by the entity, type of action (for example advisory, clarification, fine, show-cause notice, warning), details of the violation, fine amount, PCS observations/remarks, management response, and remarks. The second table is for tracking how the entity has acted on observations from previous reports, and it uses the same fields so that remediation and repeat issues can be monitored. The circular makes clear that PCS observations/remarks are mandatory whenever the compliance status is marked “No” or “NA,” so the revised ASCR is not just a yes/no certification but a more detailed exception-and-remediation reporting exercise.

rows.title: Manner of filing financial results as required under regulation 33 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India’s 15 March 2023 circular clarifies the filing format for listed entities submitting financial results under Regulation 33 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015. The Exchange observed that some companies were filing their “outcome of board meeting” PDF with extra materials such as shareholders’ letters or investor presentations, while the actual financial results, auditor’s report, and other required statements appeared later in the document. NSE is now expressly directing listed entities that the PDF filed as the outcome of the board meeting approving financial results must contain only the financial results, the auditor’s report, and the other documents/statements specifically required under Regulation 33, Part A of Schedule IV, and related circulars.

Any additional disclosures, such as a shareholders’ letter or investor presentation, cannot be embedded in the same financial-results filing and must instead be made through a separate announcement. The circular does not introduce a new substantive reporting deadline or numerical threshold, but it does impose a filing-structure compliance requirement effective immediately upon issuance of the circular, and companies are cautioned to exercise “abundant precaution” when filing under Regulation 33. This applies to all listed companies filing financial results with the Exchange.

rows.title: Operational Guidance - Amendment to Securities and Exchange Board of India (Buy-back of Securities) Regulations, 2018 (“Buy-back Regulations”)
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated 09 March 2023 is an administrative forwarding notice to all listed companies, directing attention to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-2/P/CIR/2023/35 dated 08 March 2023, which provides “Operational Guidance” linked to amendments to the SEBI (Buy-back of Securities) Regulations, 2018. The NSE document itself does not introduce independent substantive requirements; rather, it informs listed issuers that the SEBI circular is enclosed and available on the NSE website for necessary action.

For a compliance team, the key point is that SEBI has issued operational guidance in connection with the amended buy-back framework, meaning companies considering or undertaking share buy-backs should review the SEBI circular and align their procedures with the updated regulations and implementation guidance. The notice does not specify the underlying regulatory changes, thresholds, timelines, or technical compliance steps in its own text, so those details must be taken from the referenced SEBI circular. No separate effective date is stated in the NSE communication beyond the date of the SEBI circular itself, 08 March 2023.

rows.title: Filing of Related Party Transactions (RPT) and Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) to be made available on the NEAPS (NSE Electronic Application Processing System) platform
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India has extended its NEAPS single-portal filing framework so that, in addition to equity announcements and financial results, listed companies must also use NEAPS for two more XBRL submissions: Related Party Transactions (RPT) and the Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report (BRSR). This change is set out in NSE/CML/2023/18 dated February 24, 2023, and it takes effect from February 25, 2023.  

From the effective date onward, the filing routes are specifically: **NEAPS > Common XBRL Upload > Related Party Transactions** for RPT, and **NEAPS > Common XBRL Upload > Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report** for BRSR. The circular does not change the substantive reporting content or thresholds for RPT or BRSR; it changes the filing platform/process by requiring these submissions to be made available through NEAPS as part of the Exchange’s effort to consolidate filings under one portal.  

Compliance teams should ensure that personnel responsible for statutory/stock exchange filings are prepared to submit these reports through NEAPS starting on the effective date, and should use the Exchange’s designated officer contacts available on the NEAPS portal for any filing issues or queries. The circular applies to **all listed companies**.

rows.title: Resolution of Company complaints through NEAPS
rows.summary:
This NSE circular, dated February 17, 2023 (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2023/17), applies to all listed companies and concerns the handling of investor complaints related to Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements (LODR). The Exchange states that it has introduced a new functionality on the NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) so listed companies can now view all complaints lodged against them through their own NEAPS login, rather than only receiving complaints through other exchange communication channels.

Operationally, the investor complaints module is located in NEAPS under Compliance → Disclosures → Investor Complaint Desk. Once logged in, companies can see each complaint’s complaint number, symbol, company name, complainant name, complaint date, number of pending days, and current status. The module also allows companies to export the complaint list in CSV format, and when a complaint number is opened, the full complaint details and supporting information appear under a “Complaint Details” tab, including all communications previously sent by the Exchange.

For responses, the company must use the “Company Response” function and, if making a submission, click “Update.” The company is required to upload its response file under “Company file attachment,” enter the necessary remarks in the Company Response box, then click “Submit” and confirm with “OK” to send the response to the Exchange; attachments may be uploaded as PDF, including annexures. If the company does not respond, the Exchange will issue reminder(s) at regular intervals, and the non-response status will be reflected in the complaint status display.

The circular does not create a new filing deadline for complaints, but it clearly establishes a new compliance workflow: listed companies are expected to monitor complaints in NEAPS, review Exchange communications there, and provide online responses through the portal when required. The Exchange also notes that a user manual is available for guidance, and companies needing assistance may contact the helpline at 18002660050, Option 4.

rows.title: Introduction of Issue Summary Document (ISD) and dissemination of issue advertisements.
rows.summary:
SEBI has introduced a new compliance requirement for listed entities and issuers that propose to list specified securities: they must file an Issue Summary Document (ISD) in XBRL format, and issue advertisements must be disseminated on the stock exchange’s website. This is communicated by NSE circular NSE/CML/2023/16 dated February 16, 2023, which references SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/29 dated February 15, 2023.

The document does not provide the underlying procedural details or form fields itself, but it makes clear that the new filing is mandatory and that compliance is expected immediately in line with the SEBI circular. The affected parties are all listed entities and all issuers planning to list specified securities. Compliance teams should review the SEBI circular on the NSE website to understand the exact XBRL filing requirements and the process for ensuring issue advertisements are posted on the Exchange website, and should implement internal controls so that any relevant issuance activity is captured and reported in accordance with the new framework.

rows.title: FAQ’s on filing of announcements in XBRL format on NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform
rows.summary:
NSE Circular Ref. No. **NSE/CML/2023/15 dated February 7, 2023** is addressed to all listed companies and serves as guidance on the new process for filing certain stock exchange announcements in **XBRL format on the NEAPS platform**, following the earlier circular of **January 27, 2023** and demo sessions on the subject. The circular does not create a standalone new substantive rule set, but its FAQs clarify how companies must comply during the transition from PDF-only filing to XBRL filing, including that for an initial period **both PDF and XBRL submissions are required**, after which the Exchange will separately notify the date when **XBRL-only filing** will apply and only XBRL will count for compliance. During the transition period, the **PDF submission is the compliance-relevant filing until it is accepted**, and companies must submit the **XBRL version within 24 hours of the PDF disclosure**.

The FAQs specify that if a listed company had already filed a **prior intimation of a Board meeting on or before January 28, 2023**, and later wants to add a new agenda item after that date, it must file the **additional agenda item(s) in both PDF and XBRL**. If a Board meeting already intimated is later **rescheduled**, the company must file **both the PDF and the XBRL utility** for the rescheduled meeting. If the company needs to make **two separate Reg. 29 intimations for the same meeting date**—for example, first for financial results and later for dividend—the later addition is to be treated as a **new disclosure**. For XBRL labeling, **“new”** means a fresh announcement, **“update”** means an update to an earlier announcement, and **“original”** versus **“revision”** similarly distinguish the first filing from a revised one.

The circular also identifies the specific event types for which **Outcome of Board Meeting XBRL filing** applies: **Dividend, Buyback, Bonus, and Voluntary Delisting**. For resignation-related filings, the FAQs state that **resignation of the Company Secretary and Compliance Officer** should be reported using the XBRL utility that allows multiple designations for one person, with **multiple rows** entered for each designation held by that individual. For **resignation of a statutory auditor or an independent director**, the company must first inform the resignation under the **general utility**, and then file the specific resignation details in the **relevant dedicated XBRL utility**. The FAQ also clarifies that personal data such as **PAN, email ID, and phone number** of KMPs, directors, auditors, RTAs, and similar persons **will not be disseminated on the NSE website**.

Operationally, the FAQ confirms that **NSE and BSE jointly developed the XBRL utilities**, that the XML file generated from one exchange’s utility **can be uploaded on the other exchange’s portal**, and that **all four XBRL utilities are offline utilities**. For submissions, the **PDF** for a Board meeting prior intimation must be uploaded in the **Board Meeting module on NEAPS**, while the corresponding **XBRL format filing** must be uploaded in the **Common XBRL upload module on NEAPS**. If companies encounter problems with disabled macros in the utility sheet, NSE directs them to contact **their IT department**. Finally, any queries on the subject should be addressed to NSE’s **Announcements team at takeover@nse.co.in** or via the contact details available on the NEAPS platform.

rows.title: Manner of achieving minimum public shareholding
rows.summary:
This NSE circular, dated 6 February 2023, is a forwarding notice to all listed companies advising them of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD2/P/CIR/2023/18 dated 3 February 2023, titled “Manner of achieving minimum public shareholding.” The NSE communication itself does not set out the detailed requirements, thresholds, or procedures; instead, it directs listed companies to review the attached SEBI circular and take any necessary action in line with it.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the subject matter concerns how listed entities must achieve and/or maintain the minimum public shareholding requirement under SEBI’s framework. The circular is relevant to all listed companies, and the NSE explicitly expects companies to assess the SEBI circular and implement whatever actions are required. The notice also states that the SEBI circular is available on the NSE website for reference. No separate effective date, deadline, numerical threshold, or new compliance procedure is specified in the NSE letter itself beyond the instruction to refer to the SEBI circular and act accordingly.

rows.title: Generating Awareness on Availability of Dispute Resolution Mechanism at Stock Exchanges against Listed Companies/Registrar to an Issue and Share Transfer Agents (RTAs)
rows.summary:
This notice from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited is addressed to all listed companies and forwards SEBI Letter No. SEBI/HO/OIAE/2023/03391 dated January 27, 2023. The substance of the communication is not a new substantive rule for issuers, but a direction to create awareness about the dispute resolution mechanism available at stock exchanges for complaints/disputes against listed companies and against Registrars to an Issue and Share Transfer Agents (RTAs). In other words, SEBI is asking listed entities to ensure stakeholders know that exchange-level dispute resolution is available as an avenue for grievances involving the company or its RTA.

No specific numerical thresholds, fees, penalty rates, or phased implementation schedule are stated in this notice itself, and no explicit deadline is provided in the excerpt. The only action requested is “necessary action at your end,” which indicates the listed company should review the enclosed SEBI letter and take whatever awareness or communication steps that letter requires. The notice also states that the SEBI letter dated January 27, 2023 is attached and is available on the NSE website (www.nseindia.com), so compliance teams should consult that underlying SEBI communication for the detailed operational requirements.

rows.title: Attention is drawn to rule 19A (5) of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Rules, 1957 (SCRR) pursuant to Notification dated June 18, 2021 issued Ministry of Finance (MOF)
rows.summary:

From the title alone, the only clearly recoverable point is that attention is being drawn to rule 19A(5) of the SCRR in connection with a Ministry of Finance notification dated June 18, 2021, which suggests the document is intended to alert market participants to a regulatory change affecting compliance with the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Rules.
